`README.md`:

```md
# sre-re

Reverse engineering of **Solar Realms Elite 0.994b** (Amit Patel, 1995), a
DOS BBS door game, toward a C++ remake that builds and runs on Linux:
standalone (no BBS), the Linux login as the player name, multiplayer
through a shared data directory, and several galaxies per installation.

The original source code is lost; its author writes on his
[documentation page](http://www-cs-students.stanford.edu/~amitp/Articles/SRE-Documentation.html)
that he would give it out for free if he still had it. This project
recovers the game's data formats and rules from the executable instead.

## How it was made

The reverse engineering was done with [Claude](https://claude.com/claude-code)
(Anthropic's Claude Code agent, running the Claude Opus 5.5 model) and [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea)
("Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native
binaries"). REA ran the first analysis of `SRE.EXE` through its Ghidra
provider; the full export then runs [Ghidra](https://ghidra-sre.org/)
headless directly (`tools/export.sh`). The small tools in `tools/` were
written along the way (overlay flattening, string and call annotation,
disassembly, `.II` decoding).

## Status

Analysis stage; the C++ remake has not started yet.

- **Data files:** the `.II` save format is decoded and verified on real
  files (signatures, encryption, record chain), with field layouts for
  the Empire, Galaxy, System, Player and Pirate records.
- **Game logic:** fully transcribed in `docs/game/`: the turn order,
  production, expenses, population, food and starvation, civil war, the
  bank and bonds, buying and selling, attacks, covert operations,
  diplomacy and trading, random events and the daily maintenance. The
  net worth, score and production formulas are verified against the
  original.
- **Next:** checking the remaining formulas in the original game (see
  [TESTING.md](TESTING.md)), then the C++ remake.

Recovered values that are guesses are marked as such; in the future C++
code they will carry `// RE-CHECK(<kind>): <why> [orig seg:off]` tags.

## Layout

- `docs/DESIGN.md`: decisions for the Linux remake.
- `docs/formats/`: data file formats (`II.md`) and record layouts.
- `docs/game/`: game rules recovered from the code, starting at `turn.md`.
- `docs/original-bugs.md`: bugs in the original that the remake must not
  copy.
- `tools/`: the analysis toolchain (Python and Ghidra scripts).
- `data/`: original-free data for the remake.

## Tools

The pipeline needs the original `SRE.EXE` (in `sre0994b/`), Python 3,
GNU objdump and [Ghidra](https://ghidra-sre.org/):

1. `tools/deoverlay.py` flattens the Borland VROOMM overlays into one MZ
   image that Ghidra can analyse.
2. The Ghidra scripts in `tools/ghidra_scripts/` set up the project, apply
   the Borland C++ 3.0 runtime names (`tools/rtl_names.tsv`) and export
   the listing and the decompiled C (`tools/export.sh`).
3. `tools/annotate_strings.py` and `tools/annotate_calls.py` annotate the
   export with string references and the true overlay call targets.
4. `tools/disasm.py` and `tools/fieldlabels.py` help read individual
   functions; `tools/ii_decode.py` decodes and verifies a game's `Data/`
   directory.

## Original files and analysis data

The repository also keeps the original distribution and the analysis
data, so the work can be resumed on any machine:

- `sre0994b/`: the original SRE 0.994b distribution.
- `re/unpacked/`: its unpacked contents (docs, text, screens, flavors)
  and a saved copy of the author's documentation page.
- `re/flat/`, `re/flat2/`: flattened executables (`re/flat2` has the
  correct overlay fixups) and their overlay maps.
- `re/ghidra/`: the Ghidra project (built from `re/flat`).
- `re/decomp/`: the exported listing, decompiled C and annotations.
- `re/dosbox/`: a playable copy of the game for DOSBox. Start it with
  `re/dosbox/run.sh` (from any directory). The first start installs a
  fresh galaxy from `re/dosbox/galaxy/`; the game data you then create
  (`re/dosbox/game/DATA`, `NEWS`, `BACKUP`) stays local and is not
  committed. Personal settings such as the window size go in
  `re/dosbox/dosbox.local.conf`, also not committed.
- `re/samples/`: game data snapshots used for verification.

Solar Realms Elite is Amit Patel's work; the files above are his.

## Helping with tests

The documented rules still need checks in the original game. See
[TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for the setup, how to run a test and how to
report the result, and the issues labelled
[`re-check`](https://github.com/formix/sre-re/labels/re-check).

## License

The tools and documentation in this repository are released under the
[MIT License](LICENSE). This does not cover Solar Realms Elite itself
(`sre0994b/` and the original material under `re/`).

```

`TESTING.md`:

```md
# Testing the reverse-engineered rules in the original game

The game rules in `docs/game/` were read from the disassembly of SRE.EXE.
Many are tagged `RE-CHECK`: they still need to be confirmed by playing the
original game. Each such check is a GitHub issue with the
[`re-check`](https://github.com/formix/sre-re/labels/re-check)
label. This page explains how to set up the game, run a test and report the
result so that it can be compared with the documented formulas.

## 1. Setup

1. **Get the repository** and install DOSBox 0.74 (`sudo apt install dosbox`
   on Debian/Ubuntu). The game itself is already in `re/dosbox/game/`. The
   first time the game is started (by `re/dosbox/run.sh` or
   `tools/start-test.sh`), a fresh galaxy named "Test" is installed from
   `re/dosbox/galaxy/`; your empires and turns then stay on your machine
   (the game data is not committed).
2. **Start DOSBox** with `re/dosbox/run.sh` (it works from any directory
   and uses `re/dosbox/dosbox.conf`, which mounts the game with a relative
   path). If the window is too small or too large, create
   `re/dosbox/dosbox.local.conf` (not committed) with your size, keeping a
   4:3 ratio:

   ```
   [sdl]
   windowresolution=1200x900
   ```

   Alt+Enter toggles full screen.
3. **Playing outside a test:** `re/dosbox/run.sh` opens DOSBox on drive
   `C:` (the game directory). Type `SRE` to play as the last empire played,
   or `PLAY` to choose the empire: it asks for a name (a new name creates a
   new empire), then starts the game.
   - **A second empire** (for treaty, trade and attack tests): quit the
     game, type `PLAY` and enter a different name.
   - New empires are **protected** for their first turns: they cannot trade,
     attack or be attacked until protection ends. To end it at once
     (tests #5–#8), close DOSBox and run `tools/end_protection.py`.
4. **More turns today:** the game gives each empire a day's turns once a
   real day has passed. To start a new game day at once, close DOSBox and
   run `tools/next_day.py` (or `tools/next_day.py 3` for three days): it
   moves the galaxy's clocks back, which for the game is the same as the
   days passing (new turns, protection used up a day faster). Do not use
   `faketime` for this: the game would keep the fake date and give no
   turns until the real date catches up.
5. **Starting over with a fresh galaxy:** delete `re/dosbox/game/DATA`,
   `NEWS` and `BACKUP`; the template is installed again at the next start.
   (A real `SRE RESET` is not needed. If you ever run one, the original's
   Y2K bug requires a date before 12 December 1999:
   `faketime '1999-01-14' re/dosbox/run.sh`, then `SRE RESET`;
   `docs/original-bugs.md`.)
6. **Unregistered limits:** the bank (loans, bonds) and the lottery are
   disabled in this copy. Tests that need them say so.

## 2. Running a test

Read the issue's **Test** section (the **Prediction** is for reference
only: you do not need to judge the result). Then, from the repository
folder:

1. **Start the test:**

   ```
   tools/start-test.sh <issue#>
   ```

   DOSBox opens with the game started as the last empire you played (the
   first time, it asks for your empire name).
2. **Play all the test steps**, pressing **Ctrl+F5 on every screen that
   shows messages or numbers**, before pressing a key to continue (one
   screenshot per page when a screen scrolls). Play the whole test in one
   go, even over several turns or empires (to switch empire, quit the game,
   type `PLAY` and enter the other name).

   The game writes its files only when you quit it, not at the end of
   each turn. So when the Test section says **snapshot**, quit the game
   to the `C:\>` prompt and type `SRE` to continue: the copy is recorded
   automatically.
3. **When the test is over, quit the game and type `exit`** (or close the
   DOSBox window). The script then saves the result in one file,
   `re/samples/issue<#>.zip`, and opens the issue page and the folder
   holding the zip.
4. **Report:** drag the zip into a new comment on the issue (section 3).

That is all: the script records a copy in the background every time the
game writes its files (each time you quit it), picks up the screenshots by
date, and checks each copy. To start over, run
`tools/start-test.sh <issue#>` again.

Without the script (e.g. on Windows), zip the game's `DATA` and `NEWS`
folders before and after the test and attach those zips and the
screenshots instead.

## 3. Reporting the result

Post **one comment on the issue** with the template below and attach
`re/samples/issue<#>.zip` (drag it into the comment box). It holds the game
data before and after each step and the screenshots, so nothing else needs
to be attached or described.

````markdown
### Result

- **What I did:** (only what the screenshots cannot show, e.g. "fed
  people 900 of 1000 megatons, answered No to reconsider")
- **Anything unexpected:** ...

**Attachment:** issue<#>.zip
````

If you cannot attach the zip, screenshots alone are still valuable;
include one of the status screen before and one after the turn.

## 4. What happens next

The maintainer runs the analysis with Claude Code on the attached zip:
the screenshots are read for the messages and numbers, and the snapshots
are decoded (`tools/ii_decode.py`, `tools/check_turn.py`)
and compared with the documented formulas and the prediction. Then, for
each difference, the maintainer decides either to **fix** the
documentation (the reverse-engineered rule was wrong) or to **accept** it
as an intended difference of the C++ port. The decision and its reasons
are posted as a comment on the issue, the documentation and the
`RE-CHECK` tags are updated (`docs/game/verification.md` records what was
verified), and the issue is closed.

```

`cpp20-coding-rules.md`:

```md
# C++20 Coding Standard

## 1. General philosophy

The goal is to produce code that is:

- readable before being clever;
- robust before being optimized;
- simple before being generic;
- maintainable over several years by a team.

When in doubt, choose the solution that is easiest to understand.

---

## 2. Language standard

- Use **C++20**.
- Enable all compiler warnings.
- Compile without warnings.
- Treat warnings as errors.

---

## 3. Variable scope

- Declare a variable as late as possible.
- Declare a variable as close as possible to its first use.
- Limit the scope of variables to what is strictly necessary.

---

## 4. Initialization

- Every variable must be initialized when it is declared.
- Initialize immediately with a valid value.
- Class and struct members are initialized with default member initializers.

Example:

```cpp
i32 count = 0;
const auto id = generate_id();
```

---

## 4.1 Integer types

### Rule

Use the fixed-width types from `<cstdint>`.

### Mandatory project aliases

```cpp
using i8  = std::int8_t;
using i16 = std::int16_t;
using i32 = std::int32_t;
using i64 = std::int64_t;

using u8  = std::uint8_t;
using u16 = std::uint16_t;
using u32 = std::uint32_t;
using u64 = std::uint64_t;
```

### Floating-point types

```cpp
using f32 = float;
using f64 = double;
```

### Avoid

```cpp
short
unsigned short
long
unsigned long
long long
unsigned long long
```

---

## 4.2 Use of the `char` type

### Rule

The `char` type is reserved exclusively for representing characters.

### Correct

```cpp
char c = 'A';
std::string name = "Jean";
```

### Forbidden

```cpp
char flags;
char counter;
char buffer[1024];
```

### Binary data

Use:

```cpp
u8
```

or

```cpp
std::byte
```

### Principle

> `char` represents text.
>
> `u8` represents an 8-bit integer.
>
> `std::byte` represents raw binary data.

---

## 5. Const by default

Every variable that does not change must be declared `const`.

```cpp
const auto user = load_user();
```

---

## 6. Resource management (RAII)

### Definition

**RAII** (*Resource Acquisition Is Initialization*) is the principle that:

> A resource is acquired when an object is constructed and released automatically when it is destroyed.

The lifetime of the resource must be identical to the lifetime of the object that owns it.

### Resources covered

- memory;
- files;
- network sockets;
- mutexes;
- connections;
- system handles.

### Rule

Every resource must be managed by a RAII object.

### Examples

```cpp
std::ifstream file("data.txt");
```

```cpp
std::scoped_lock lock(mutex);
```

```cpp
auto object = std::make_unique<MyObject>();
```

### Forbidden

```cpp
new
delete
malloc
free
```

unless a documented exception applies.

### Rule of thumb

When the code contains:

```cpp
open / close
lock / unlock
new / delete
malloc / free
```

look for a RAII solution first.

---

## 7. Memory ownership

### Prefer

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<T>
```

### Use only when necessary

```cpp
std::shared_ptr<T>
```

### Non-owning references

```cpp
T&
const T&
T*
```

---

## 8. Containers

Prefer:

```cpp
std::vector
std::array
std::string
std::map
std::unordered_map
```

Avoid raw arrays.

---

## 9. Function parameters

Read-only:

```cpp
void process(const User& user);
```

Character string:

```cpp
void print(std::string_view text);
```

Collection:

```cpp
void process(std::span<const Item> items);
```

---

## 10. Value types

Favor simple value types.

```cpp
struct Point
{
    f64 x = 0.0;
    f64 y = 0.0;
};
```

---

## 11. Inheritance

### Rule

Prefer composition.

### Allowed inheritance

- polymorphic interfaces;
- obvious "is-a" relationships.

### Forbidden

- multiple inheritance with state;
- deep hierarchies.

---

## 12. Composition

Composition is the preferred mechanism for reuse.

```cpp
class Database
{
private:
    Connection connection;
};
```

---

## 13. Error handling

When a value may be absent and the caller does not need to know why, return:

```cpp
std::optional<T>
```

When the caller needs to know why an operation failed, return a `std::error_code`, or a project-defined result type that carries either the value or the error.

Use exceptions only for exceptional errors.

---

## 14. Use of `auto`

Use `auto` when the type is obvious.

```cpp
auto ptr = std::make_unique<User>();
```

Readability comes first.

---

## 15. Templates

Use templates for simple genericity.

Constrain templates with concepts instead of SFINAE (`std::enable_if`).

```cpp
template <std::integral T>
T clamp_to_zero(T value);
```

Avoid complex metaprogramming.

---

## 16. Loops

Prefer:

```cpp
for (const auto& item : items)
{
    process(item);
}
```

---

## 17. Functions

A function must:

- do one thing only;
- have an explicit name;
- limit side effects.

---

## 18. Features to avoid

```cpp
goto
union
reinterpret_cast
dynamic_cast
volatile
```

Alternatives:

- instead of `union`, use `std::variant`;
- instead of `reinterpret_cast` to reread an object's bytes as another type, use `std::bit_cast`.

Complex macros are forbidden.

---

## 19. Recommended standard library

```txt
<cstdint>
<cstddef>
<string>
<string_view>
<vector>
<array>
<map>
<unordered_map>
<set>
<unordered_set>
<memory>
<optional>
<variant>
<system_error>
<span>
<concepts>
<bit>
<algorithm>
<ranges>
<chrono>
<filesystem>
<thread>
<mutex>
<condition_variable>
```

---

## 20. Motto

> Initialize immediately, limit scope, use RAII, favor composition, make types explicit, and write obvious code.

`docs/DESIGN.md`:

```md
# SRE for Linux — design decisions

Goal: a C++ reimplementation of Solar Realms Elite 0.994b (Amit Patel, 1995)
that builds on Linux, runs standalone (no BBS), uses the Linux login as the
player name, and stays multiplayer through shared game data.

## Original program (reverse-engineering facts)

- `SRE.EXE`: Borland C++ 3.0, large memory model, 16-bit real mode.
- Borland VROOMM overlays: 45 overlay modules (~237 KB code, 435 entry points)
  in an `FBOV` block appended at file offset `0x2DF60`.
  `tools/deoverlay.py` flattens them into one MZ image for static analysis.
- Text resources load at runtime from `TEXT/`, `SCREENS/`, `DATA/` and
  `RESOURCE.DAT`; many more strings are hard-coded in the executable.
- The original was single-player-at-a-time (lock file `INUSE.SR`), with up to
  25 empires per galaxy and a daily maintenance run.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Language / build | C++20, CMake, system SQLite3 |
| Player identity | Current Linux login name |
| Shared data | `/var/games/sre`, group `games`, mode 2775; binary installed setgid `games`. Path overridable by config/env for development. |
| Galaxies | Multi-galaxy: `sre [galaxy]`. One SQLite file per galaxy, `/var/games/sre/galaxies/<slug>.db` (slug = lowercased name, non-alphanumerics → `-`; display name kept as typed). Each galaxy has its own lock, RNG state, maintenance clock and settings. A user may own one empire per galaxy. Without a name, `sre` enters the default galaxy set in the system config. |
| Galaxy names | `sre reset` without a name picks an unused name from `data/galaxy-names.txt` (100 names: real galaxies, no `M###` catalogue numbers, plus invented ones). |
| Concurrency | Per galaxy: exclusive lock (`flock`), like `INUSE.SR`, plus a waiting queue: a second user sees who is playing and may wait. Different galaxies can be played at the same time. |
| Storage | SQLite. Original binary layouts are recovered for field semantics only; a DOS→SQLite importer may exist as a test tool. |
| Terminal UI | Direct ANSI output + termios raw input; CP437→UTF-8 conversion so original `.ANS`/`.TXT` screens display unchanged. |
| Maintenance | Lazy catch-up of missed intervals on launch (inside the lock), plus `sre maint` for cron. |
| Dates (Y2K fix) | All times are 64-bit (`std::chrono`, `int64_t` seconds). The original rejected any galaxy reset after 1999-12-12 (`6c37:02c9`, `docs/original-bugs.md`); the remake has no date window and must work past 2038. A unit test resets a galaxy with a clock set after 2038 and plays a turn. |
| Randomness | Modern, seedable, deterministic PRNG (no true-random sources such as `std::random_device`). One RNG object is passed explicitly to game logic, never global. Range mapping is implemented in-house rather than with `std::*_distribution`, so a given seed gives identical results across compilers and standard libraries. Unit tests always seed explicitly and assert exact outcomes. In play, the RNG state is persisted in the galaxy's SQLite database: it is seeded once, at galaxy creation (`sre reset`, from the clock or from `--seed`), is never re-seeded afterwards, and every session resumes from the saved state and writes it back. A copy of the database plus the same keystrokes therefore replays a session exactly. Not a replica of Borland `rand()`, so no replay against the original. |
| Registration | Everything unlocked; no nag screens or key code. |
| Text | Two string catalogs with stable IDs: `original` (Amit Patel's text, including strings hard-coded in `SRE.EXE`) and `rewritten` (new text). Chosen at compile time (CMake option). The original files are committed (decision of 2026-10-17); the `original` catalog may be committed too, and stays separable from `rewritten`. Context: the author's documentation page says "If I had the source code, I'd give it out for free, but I don't have it anymore" (SRE-Documentation.html). |
| Flavors and settings | Original `RESOURCE.DAT` / `TRANSLAT.DAT` formats and alternate screens supported. Global defaults in the system config; per-galaxy overrides (flavor, game options) chosen at creation and stored in the galaxy DB. |
| Admin | `sre reset [galaxy]` (create or wipe), `sre sysop <galaxy>`, `sre maint [galaxy]` (all galaxies if omitted), restricted to root or an admin group from the config. Sysop editor keeps the original menu UI. |

## Integer types

All integers use `<cstdint>` fixed-width names with the same width as in the
original Borland C++ 3.0 16-bit build:

| Borland C++ 3.0 | Port |
|---|---|
| `char` (signed by default) used as a number | `int8_t` |
| `unsigned char` | `uint8_t` |
| `int`, `short` | `int16_t` |
| `unsigned int`, `unsigned short` | `uint16_t` |
| `long` | `int32_t` |
| `unsigned long` | `uint32_t` |

Rules:

- Plain `int`, `short`, `long`, `unsigned` are not used in game code. A check
  script run by CTest rejects them in `src/` (outside library-interop shims).
- Widths come from the decompiled code (Ghidra reports exact operand sizes), not
  from guesses about the value range.
- C++ promotes 16-bit operands to 32-bit `int`, while the original computed in 16
  bits. Where that changes a result (an intermediate that overflows before being
  widened, compared or divided, or `int16_t`/`uint16_t` mixed so that Borland's
  usual arithmetic conversions picked unsigned), the code reproduces the
  original explicitly with helpers such as `wrap16()` / `as_u16()`, with a
  comment naming the original function address.
- Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wsign-compare` so
  implicit narrowing and sign mixing are visible.
- Exceptions, kept at the boundary: `char` for text, `bool`, `size_t` for
  container sizes and indices, and whatever types SQLite and POSIX APIs require.
- Floating point: Borland used x87 80-bit intermediates; any `double` formula
  whose result is rounded or truncated gets a unit test at its boundary values.

## Marking reverse-engineering guesses

The C++ port is written by hand from the decompiled output, and some readings
are uncertain (for example which string a 16-bit offset refers to, a field's
type, or a function's argument list). Every such guess carries a tagged comment
at the exact spot:

```cpp
// RE-CHECK(<kind>): <what was guessed and why> [orig <seg:off>]
```

- `<kind>`: `string`, `type`, `width`, `signature`, `formula`, `flow`, `field`, ...
- `[orig seg:off]`: address in the Ghidra project of the flattened `SRE.EXE`, so
  the original instructions can be inspected.
- `grep -rn RE-CHECK src/` lists everything still to verify. Remove the tag once
  the behaviour is confirmed by testing.

Testing and fixing happen on the readable C++ code, not on the intermediate
decompiled C.

## Repository layout

- `src/` — the C++ port
- `tools/` — reverse-engineering scripts (`deoverlay.py`, Ghidra scripts)
- `docs/` — recovered specifications and design notes
- `data/` — original-free game data (e.g. `galaxy-names.txt`)
- `README.md`, `LICENSE` (MIT, for this repository's own tools and docs)
- `sre0994b/`, `re/` — original distribution and analysis outputs (committed)

```

`docs/formats/II.md`:

```md
# `.II` data file format (SRE 0.994b)

The game state lives in `Data/*.II`, with copies in `Backup/*.II` made by the
daily maintenance (overlay function `5680:0c52`, which only copies files):

`System`, `Empire`, `Galaxy`, `Player`, `Pirate`, `Battles`, `Trading`,
`CovertOp`, `Message`, `Report`, `Event`.

None ship with the game; `SRE RESET` creates them. Everything marked
**verified** below was checked against files from a real `SRE RESET` run in
DOSBox (`tools/ii_decode.py` decodes and verifies a whole `Data` directory).

## Overview

There are three kinds of file:

| File | Kind | Record size | Signed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYSTEM.II` | plain, one record | 322 (`0x142`) | — |
| `PLAYER.II` | plain, one record per player | 114 (`0x72`) | — |
| `GALAXY.II` | encrypted, one record (whole file) | file size (966 after reset) | `SYSTEM.II` @ `0x12A` |
| `EMPIRE.II` | encrypted, one record per empire slot | 764 | `GALAXY` @ `0x54 + 24*i` |
| `PIRATE.II` | encrypted, one record per pirate slot | 262 | `GALAXY` @ `0x2AC + 24*i` |
| `BATTLES`, `TRADING`, `COVERTOP`, `MESSAGE`, `REPORT`, `EVENT` | probably the stream format below | — | in-record |

The signature chain is **verified**: the System record holds Galaxy's
signature, and the decrypted Galaxy record holds one signature per Empire and
Pirate record. A reset game had 25 empire slots and 9 pirate slots (19100 and
2358 bytes). Tampering with any file breaks its own signature, and since the
signatures are random-keyed and stored in the parent file, records cannot be
copied between games or slots.

Each record is the raw memory image of a C++ object (Borland large model,
16-bit `int`, little-endian). Field layouts are documented per class as they
are recovered.

## Record files (code segment `2144`)

All `.II` files are accessed through one small class (`0x8C` bytes,
constructor `2144:096f`):

| Offset | Size | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | 128 | `name` — path |
| 0x80 | 2 | `fd` — DOS handle, -1 when closed |
| 0x82 | 2 | `recsize` |
| 0x84 | 2 | `error` — last errno, 1 on short read/write |
| 0x86 | 4 | cached file position (-1 = unknown) |
| 0x8A | 1 | `xor_key` |
| 0x8B | 1 | `xor_len` (0 is treated as 1) |

Constructor arguments: `(this, name, recsize, xor_key, xor_len)`.

- `count()` (`2144:0f6d`) = file length / `recsize`.
- `read(recno, n, buf)` (`2144:0be7`) seeks to `recno * recsize` and reads
  `n` records; `write` (`2144:0d28`) is the mirror.
- Both pass the buffer through `2144:0b5c`, which XORs byte `i` of each
  record with `xor_key + (i % xor_len)`. It is skipped when `xor_key == 0`
  and `xor_len == 1`, which is what every `.II` file seen so far uses, so
  this layer does nothing in practice.

Galaxy is read by opening the file with `recsize = 1` to get its length, then
reopening with `recsize` = that length and reading record 0 (loader
`6c37:0349`).

## Signature (24 bytes) — verified

| Offset | Size | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | 4 | `sum` — `checksum16` of the plaintext, as uint32 (high word always 0) |
| 0x04 | 4 | `crc` — `crc32` of the plaintext |
| 0x08 | 8 | `key` — initial encryption key (random, from Borland `rand()`) |
| 0x10 | 8 | `final_key` — key state after encrypting the whole buffer |

Code: constructor `14f6:000f` (zeroes it), make `14f6:005c`, verify
`14f6:0147`, decrypt-in-place `14f6:01cb`. Algorithms in overlay `741f`.

## Algorithms — verified

### `crc32` (`741f:009a`, table `741f:0000`)

Reflected CRC-32, polynomial `0xEDB88320`, initial value `0xFFFFFFFF`, **no
final XOR**:

```
crc = 0xFFFFFFFF
for b in buf: crc = (crc >> 8) ^ table[(crc ^ b) & 0xFF]
```

### `checksum16` (`741f:0130`)

```
a = 0; s = 0; r = 0            // all 16-bit
for b in buf:
    r ^= b; r = ror16(r, 1)
    a += b
    s += a
return (r << 16) | s           // computed in 16 bits: r << 16 == 0
```

The original evaluates `r << 16` in a 16-bit register, so the rotate-XOR part
is lost and the result is just `s` (high word 0). Any reader must reproduce
this, or every checksum will mismatch.

### Encryption (`741f:0196` encrypt, `741f:028c` decrypt + verify)

An XOR stream cipher with an 8-byte evolving key. With `k[8]` = `key` and
`c` = 0 (uint8):

```
for i in 0 .. len-1:
    j = i & 7
    p = plaintext byte i
    out[i] = p ^ k[j]
    k[j] = rol8(k[j], 3) ^ c ^ p
    c = c + 7  (mod 256)
final_key = k
```

Decryption is the same with `p = in[i] ^ k[j]`; after the last byte, `k` must
equal `final_key`, otherwise the record fails the "data security check".

## Known fields

Only what is obvious from the reset sample so far; full layouts come from
the class code.

- `SYSTEM` (322): `0x00` char[] (`"formix"` in the sample), `0x40` char[]
  (`"amazing"`), `0xD0` bank name (`"First Intergalactic Bank of The Solar
  Realm"`), `0x120` and `0x124` two `time_t` (Unix seconds), `0x12A` Galaxy
  signature.
- `GALAXY`: `0x00` galaxy name (char[], `"Andromedae"`), `0x40`..`0x53`
  `time_t` values, `0x54` 25 Empire signatures, `0x2AC` 9 Pirate signatures,
  then settings from `0x384`.
- `PLAYER` (114): `0x02` user name (char[32], upper case), `0x22` name
  (char[32]), `0x42` 16 char/attribute pairs (`20 07` = blank, grey), `0x62`
  two `time_t`.
- `EMPIRE` (764): `0x00` int16 controlling player (-1 = free slot), `0x24` two
  `time_t`, then starting values (planet counts, resources) from `0x30`.

## Stream format (code segment `1629`, "streamfile") — not yet seen

The persistence code in segment `1629` reads and writes a stream of
self-describing objects. It is probably used by the files that were still
empty after the reset (Battles, Trading, CovertOp, Message, Report, Event);
this is **unverified**.

```
record := header[80] data[header.size]
```

| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | 2 | `size` | int16, length of `data`. Negative: record is skipped ("negative packet size"). |
| 0x02 | 24 | `name_sig` | signature of the class-name field |
| 0x1A | 30 | `class_name` | NUL-terminated C++ class name, encrypted with `name_sig` |
| 0x38 | 24 | `data_sig` | signature of `data` |

Reading (`1629:0102`): read the header; decrypt and verify `class_name`
("header corrupted, skipping record" on failure); create the object by name
(factory `1629:004e`, "couldn't match class header {...}"); call its virtual
size method (vtable + 8), zero the object after its 2-byte vtable pointer,
read `size` bytes over it at `object + 2`, then decrypt and verify ("Data
security check failed"). Files are written to `<name>.$$$` and renamed
(`1629:07c7`).

## Open points

- Field layouts of every class.
- Whether the slot counts (25 empires, 9 pirates) are fixed or come from a
  Galaxy setting.
- Confirm the stream format on non-empty Battles/Message/... files.
- Exact use of `rand()` to derive keys (`14f6:005c`); only needed to
  reproduce files byte for byte.

## Clocks after a reset

A reset writes the current time into SYSTEM `+0x120`/`+0x124`, GALAXY
`+0x40`, `+0x44`, `+0x48`, `+0x3BA`, EMPIRE `+0x24`/`+0x28` of every slot
and PIRATE `+0x22` of every team, over a few seconds (values within about
a minute of each other). `tools/galaxy_now.py` moves all but SYSTEM's to the
present and re-signs the files; `re/dosbox/prepare.sh` runs it when it
installs the galaxy template, which had to be reset under a 1999 date.

```

`docs/formats/empire.md`:

```md
# `Empire` record (764 bytes, `EMPIRE.II`)

One record per empire slot (25 in a reset game), stored encrypted in
`EMPIRE.II` (see `II.md`). In memory the records form an array of `0x2FC`
(764) byte objects reached through the far pointer at `DS:c92e`.

The layout is **byte-packed** (Borland default alignment 1): `int32_t`
fields can sit at odd offsets (e.g. agents at `0x22B`). All integers are
little-endian; `int16_t` is the original `int`, `int32_t` the original `long`.

Sources:
- the sysop status window `1cf7:0009` (labels next to field reads; resident
  code, decompiled correctly);
- Empire methods in segment `1c59`;
- two real samples: `re/samples/reset1` (after `SRE RESET`) and
  `re/samples/turn5` (one empire, "Gregorious", after 5 turns), checked
  against `SRESCORE.TXT` (357 planets, score 1092, net worth 3900).

**Confidence:** *code* = the code reads/prints it under that label; *sample*
= only inferred from how the value changed between the two samples (tag
`RE-CHECK(field)` when used in the port).

## Fields

| Offset | Type | Name | Confidence | Reset → turn 5 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x000 | int16 | empire # (slot index), -1 = free slot | sample | -1 → 0 | |
| 0x002 | char[32] | empire name; empty = no empire | code + sample | "" → "Gregorious" | Player Editor `4739:1283` |
| 0x022 | int16 | controlling player # (`PLAYER.II` index), -1 = none | code | -1 → 0 | "This player is currently controlling empire" `4739:12a3` |
| 0x024 | uint32 | time_t, created? | sample | | |
| 0x028 | uint32 | time_t, last played? | sample | | |
| 0x02C | Planets[10] | planets by type, 12 bytes each | code | | `1c59:0152`, `1c59:004b` |
| 0x0EC | Treaty[25] | treaty with each other empire, 4 bytes each (below) | code | all 0 | net worth `1c59:028b`; attacks `5c5b:0000` |

| 0x188 | int32 | pollution (exatons) | code | 0 → 214 | production `4629:0000` (+ petroleum planets, − anti-pollution); subtracted in net worth |
| 0x18C | int32 | food stock (megatons) | code | | production adds food grown |
| 0x190 | int16 | violence/unrest level 0..7 (selects a status text) | code | 0 | `1c59:0740`; `1c59:002a` decrements it; drives the violence bill (`expenses.md`) |
| 0x192 | int16 | ? | sample | 0 → 61 | |
| 0x194 | int16 | turn number; < 0 = under protection | code | -20 → -15 | `1cf7` |
| 0x196 | int16 | turns used in this maintenance interval | code | 0 → 5 | `1cf7` (turns left = `DS:07e8` − this) |
| 0x198 | int16 | ? | sample | 5 → 5 | |
| 0x19A | int16 | turn at which the next Coordinator allowance is due (`civil-war.md`) | code + sample | -20 → -15 | `48cb:232d` |
| 0x19C | int32 | bank balance; negative = loan | code | 0 | `1cf7`; expenses `5e47:01e5` |
| 0x1A4 | int32 | loan payment due per year | code | | expenses `5e47:01fa` |
| 0x1AA | int8 | tax rate (%) | code | 23 | taxes = pop × rate × 3 / (state + 1) in `4629:0000`; net worth uses `pop / (rate + 10)` |
| 0x1AD | int8 | draft rate (soldiers drafted = population / 100 × rate when attacked) | code | | `3b7a:0e7a` |

| 0x1B4 | int32 | efficiency = (taxable × 1000 − bill) / planets | code | 0 → 1090 | `1cf7`; set in `5e47:09d4` |
| 0x1B8 | uint16 | option flags (Galaxy `+0x386` is OR-ed in at load) | code | | `6c37:07f2` |

| 0x1C4 | uint8 | event flags: bit 0 planned civil war (unpaid planets), bit 1 insurgent riots (starving people, `512e:0c47`), bit 2 ?, bit 3 army shortfall (unpaid or underfed military; verified for underfed, issue #2) | code | | `44e1:07cc`, `5e47:03f6`, `44e1:0000` |

## Starting values (`48cb:0254`), verified

A new or free slot is initialized by `48cb:0254`; all 25 slots of the
`reset1` sample hold exactly these values. Everything not listed is 0.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| empire # `+0x000`, controlling player `+0x022` | -1 |
| name `+0x002` | "" |
| time stamps `+0x024`, `+0x028` | now |
| Petroleum (count, base, current) | 0, 1900, 1900 |
| Education | 3, 17, 39 |
| Tourism | 9, 2650, 3100 |
| Food | 1, 46, 53 |
| Research | 1, 9, 11 |
| Ore | 9, 2200, 2500 |
| Government | 1, 2, 3 |
| Urban | 3, 200, 210 |
| Supply | 0, 11, 15 |
| Anti-pollution | 0, 10, 10 |
| army effectiveness `+0x170` | 100 |
| money `+0x17C` | 10,000 |
| population `+0x184` | 40 |
| turn `+0x194`, `+0x19A` | −(Galaxy turns of protection `+0x3A0`), -20 without a Galaxy |
| `+0x198` | Galaxy turns per interval `+0x39E` (5 without a Galaxy) |
| tax rate `+0x1AA` | 23 |
| draft rate `+0x1AD` | 5 |
| supply allocation `+0x297..+0x29C` | 20, 20, 20, 20, 10, 10 |
| inactive days left `+0x2A1` | 4 (refilled from `InactiveTimeOut` when playing) |

So a new empire has 27 planets. The percentage fields are clamped to
0..100 when set (`48cb:0bc2`..).

## `Treaty` (4 bytes, at `+0x0EC + 4 × other empire`)

Bit fields over the 4 bytes (byte 0 is the lowest):

| Bits | Field |
|---|---|
| 0..7 | days left on the treaty (byte 0; −1 per day in the maintenance; net worth adds `(x + 5) / 3`) |
| 8..12 | treaty kind (below) |
| 13..17 | pending action: 0 none, 1 Proposed, 2 Rejected, 3 Accepted, 4 Treaty Broken (labels of "View Relations"; `diplomacy.md`) |
| 18..24 | heavy cruisers sent by this ally when you are attacked, % |
| 25..31 | soldiers sent by this ally when you are attacked, % |

Kinds (names from `DS:1ca9`): 0 No Relations, 1 Neutrality/Peace Treaty,
2 Free Trade Agreement (pays trade taxes, `production.md`), 3 Minor
Alliance Pact (20 % / 20 %), 4 Armed Defense Pact (60 % soldiers), 5
Cruiser Protection Plan (60 % cruisers), 6 Total Defense Pact (40 % /
40 %), 7 Custom Treaty. The percentages are what the attack code writes
(`3b7a:0884`); `RE-CHECK(field)`: which 7-bit field is soldiers and which
cruisers follows from the Armed Defense / Cruiser Protection names.

## `Planets` (12 bytes)

The 10 entries are in the order of the type letters at `DS:9d69`,
`PETFROGUSA`; methods accept either the index 0..9 or the letter.

| Index | Letter | Type | Offset |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | P | Petroleum | 0x2C |
| 1 | E | Education | 0x38 |
| 2 | T | Tourism | 0x44 |
| 3 | F | Food | 0x50 |
| 4 | R | Research | 0x5C |
| 5 | O | Ore | 0x68 |
| 6 | G | Government | 0x74 |
| 7 | U | Urban | 0x80 |
| 8 | S | Supply | 0x8C |
| 9 | A | Anti-pollution | 0x98 |

| Offset | Type | Field | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0 | int32 | count | code (`1c59:004b` sums it; 357 in the sample = score file) |
| 0x4 | int32 | base production per planet (constant after reset: 1900, 17, 2650, 46, 9, 2200, 2, 200, 11, 10) | sample |
| 0x8 | int32 | current production per planet; production multiplies the count by it (e.g. Ore 2500 → 2455) | code (`4629:0000`) |

Field 0x8 drifts toward field 0x4 by a thirtieth of the gap each turn
(`docs/game/production.md`, verified).

The table at `DS:9d48` holds the offsets as `0x2D + 12*i`, and the code
subtracts 1; an index outside 0..9 prints "FATAL ERROR @Empire::Planets"
and exits.

## Computed values

- Planets = sum of `Planets[i].count` (`1c59:004b`).
- Net worth (`1c59:028b`), **verified**: gives 3900 on the turn-5 sample,
  as in `SRESCORE.TXT`. All arithmetic is 32-bit signed, divisions truncate
  toward zero (Borland `LDIV@`):

  ```
  nw = 0
  for i in 0..24:                       # relation entries at 0x0EC
      kind = byte[0xED + 4i] & 0x1F
      if kind != 0:
          nw += (byte[0xEC + 4i] + 5) / 3
          if kind != 1 and kind != 2: nw += 1
  nw += planets * (10 - state)          # state = violence level, int16 0x190
  nw += money / 100000                  # 0x17C
  nw += agents * 7                      # 0x22B
  nw += soldiers + fighters             # 0x154, 0x158
  nw += cruisers * 3 + light_cruisers * 3   # 0x160, 0x2F0
  nw += defense_stations * 2            # 0x15C
  nw += carriers * 3 + generals * 2     # 0x164, 0x168
  nw += population / (int8[0x1AA] + 10) # 0x184
  nw += int8[0x171]                     # command ship byte
  nw += bank / 110000 - pollution       # 0x19C, 0x188
  nw += int32[0x16C] / 2
  return max(nw, 0)
  ```

- Petroleum price, probably (`5221:03b4`): over all 25 slots,
  `300 * Σ planets / (Σ petroleum planets + 10)`, clamped to 700..100000
  and stored as a long at `+0x3B6` of the object passed in.
  `RE-CHECK(field)`: that object is not obviously the Galaxy (its long at
  `0x3B6` is 2502 in the turn-5 sample, while the formula gives 863).

```

## Validity check (`6c37:02c9`)

`main` treats the game as "not reset" unless both time stamps are
strictly between 315,000,000 and 945,000,000 seconds (1979-12-25 ..
1999-12-12), the registered flag is 0..5 and the BBS name is not empty.
The upper bound is the original's Y2K bug (`docs/original-bugs.md`).

```

`docs/game/attacks.md`:

```md
# Attacks and covert operations (turn steps 14 and 20)

Transcribed from the disassembly, **not checked against the game**:
`RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in `production.md`;
`rnd(k)` = `rand() * k / 32768`.

## Attack menu (step 20, `508f:0121`)

"Attack Options": Conventional Invasion (`3b7a:0325`), Guerilla Ambush
(`545d:0000`), Pirate Raid (`5fdf:0297`), Spy on Pirates (`5fdf:19d9`),
Nuclear Offensive (`5c5b:060b`), Chemical Warfare (`5c5b:0f19`), Psionic
Attack (`5c5b:1862`). The target is chosen with `5221:1539` / `14d3`;
"The Galactic Coordinator will not let you attack more than N times per M
turns": attacks (other than pirate raids) are counted in Empire `+0x229`
and refused once it reaches the resource `Attacks.Maximum` (default -1 =
no limit; `508f:04b9`). Resources `Attacks.Conventional`, `Guerilla`,
`PirateRaid`, `PirateSpy`, `Nuclear`, `Chemical` enable each type
(`RESOURCE.DOC`; for nuclear and chemical they control acquiring the
weapons, not using them). Nuclear and
chemical attacks anger the Coordinator. Only the conventional invasion is
transcribed so far.

## Conventional invasion (`3b7a:0325`)

`5c5b:0000` first checks that the attack is allowed. The attacker then
chooses how many soldiers, fighters, light cruisers and heavy cruisers to
send ("Take how many ...?"; enough generals and carriers are needed to
lead them, "You do not have enough generals and carriers to lead all your
forces into battle"). The treaty between the two empires is then reset
(`3b7a:0884`, same rule as below).

### Forces

Four pools per side, paired:

| Pool | Attacker | Defender |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | soldiers sent | soldiers + drafted + allies' soldiers |
| 1 | fighters sent | defense stations |
| 2 | heavy cruisers sent | heavy cruisers + allies' cruisers |
| 3 | light cruisers sent | light cruisers |

The defender drafts `drafted = population / 100 * draft_rate` soldiers
(Empire int8 `+0x1AD`; "N soldiers are drafted") and loses `drafted / 10`
million people. Allies send soldiers and heavy cruisers ("'s allies send
N soldiers and N heavy cruisers", `3b7a:0bc4`):

```
for each live empire e (all 25 slots):
    t = e.treaty[defender]                  # the ally's own entry
    if t.status == 0:                       # no proposal/break pending
        ally_soldiers[e] = e.soldiers / 100 * t.soldier_pct        # bits 25..31
        ally_cruisers[e] = e.heavy_cruisers / 100 * t.cruiser_pct  # bits 18..24
```

The treaty kind is not tested: the percentages are only non-zero for
defense treaties (Minor Alliance 20/20, Armed Defense 60/0, Cruiser
Protection 0/60, Total Defense 40/40, Custom as set). An ally whose own
army is busy elsewhere still sends its full share (nothing is reserved).

For each pool pair, a hit removes `chunk[i] = (attacker[i] +
defender[i]) / 50 + 1` units (computed once, before the battle).

### Battle

```
init_att = sum(attacker pools); init_def = sum(defender pools)
round = 0
repeat:
    # eight duels; "loses(order)" removes chunk[i] from the first pool in
    # `order` that is not empty (3b7a:0035), never below 0
    if round >= 3 and rnd(200) < defender.army_eff + 90:
        attacker loses (soldiers, heavy, fighters, light)
    if round >= 3 and rnd(200) < attacker.army_eff + 90:
        defender loses (soldiers, heavy, stations, light)
    if round >= 2 and rnd(200) < 100:
        attacker loses (fighters, soldiers, heavy, light)
    if round >= 2 and rnd(200) < 100:
        defender loses (stations, soldiers, heavy, light)
    if round >= 5 and rnd(200) < defender.cmd_ship / 2 + 50:
        attacker loses (heavy, DEFENDER light, fighters, soldiers)   # see note
    if round >= 5 and rnd(200) < attacker.cmd_ship / 2 + 50:
        defender loses (heavy, light, stations, soldiers)
    if rnd(200) < 100:
        attacker loses (light, heavy, fighters, soldiers)
    if rnd(200) < 100:
        defender loses (light, heavy, stations, soldiers)
    round += 1
until round > 77
   or sum(attacker pools) <= init_att / 10
   or sum(defender pools) <= init_def / 10
```

`army_eff` is Empire int8 `+0x170`; `cmd_ship` is the signed byte at
`+0x171` (`(x - sign) >> 1`, i.e. division by 2 toward zero).

Note: in the fifth duel the original passes a pointer to the
**defender's** light-cruiser pool in the attacker's loss list
(`3b7a:1289`), so when the attacker has no heavy cruisers left the
defender loses light cruisers instead. `RE-CHECK(bug)`: probably a
typo in the original; keep it for fidelity or fix it, to decide when
testing (`docs/original-bugs.md`).

### Outcome

```
score = 0
for each pool pair (a, d):
    score += (a > 0) + (a > 2*d) - (d > 0) - (d > 2*a)
if score > 0:                                  # attacker wins
    score *= 2
    if attacker.net_worth > defender.net_worth and
       attacker.planets > defender.planets:
        score = score / 3 + 1                  # big empires capture less
    divisor = max(20 / score + 1, 3)
    for each planet type t:
        take = defender.Planets[t].count / divisor
        if take == 0 and count > 0: take = 1
        if take == 1 and count > 1: take = 2
        take = min(take, count)                # "pl/planets incorrect assignment"

    # top up at random to at least defender.planets / divisor in total
    while sum(take) < defender.planets / divisor:
        t = rnd(10)
        if defender.Planets[t].count > take[t]: take[t] += 1
    credits = defender.money / divisor

    attacker.army_eff -= 13;  attacker.cmd_ship -= 7          # clamped 0..100
    defender.army_eff -= 3;   defender.cmd_ship -= rnd(5) + 2
    move take[t] planets of each type and `credits` from defender to attacker
    attacker.score += defender.score * score / 10 + sum(take) * 17
    defender.score = max(defender.score - defender.score * score / 20
                         - sum(take) * 7, 0)
    if defender.planets == 0:                    # wiped out
        attacker.score += defender.score;  defender.score = 0
else:                                            # attacker loses
    attacker.cmd_ship -= rnd(7) + rnd(3) + 3
    attacker.army_eff += score                   # score <= 0
    defender.cmd_ship -= 5;  defender.army_eff -= 4
    attacker.score = max(attacker.score - (rnd(100) + 110), 0)
```

Real losses are a **third** of the battle casualties (`3b7a:1f7a`):

```
for each attacker pool: loss = (sent - remaining) / 3
attacker.generals -= (soldier_loss + 50) / 200
attacker.carriers -= min(attacker.carriers, (fighter_loss + 200) / 1000)
for each defender pool: loss = (initial - remaining) / 3
    # soldiers counted with the drafted and allied ones
```

Reports (`3f61`, also used by the other attack kinds and by the covert
set-up). The defender's report (`3f61:00cb`) depends on the battle score:

| score | "X ..." |
|---|---|
| > 10 | "demolished your empire and spread terror throughout the land!" |
| 5..10 | "invaded your empire and caused devastation!" |
| 3..4 | "caused considerable damage to your land in a fierce attack." |
| 1..2 | "attacked you and defeated your forces." |
| -2..0 | "attacked but was repelled by your forces." |
| -5..-3 | "attempted an invasion but was unable to penetrate your defenses." |
| ≤ -6 | "made a feeble attempt to invade your lands." |

The news line (`3f61:0209`): "X <verb> Y" with verb by score: > 10
"pulverized", 9..10 "devastated", 5..8 "demolished", 3..4 "invaded",
1..2 "defeated", "completely destroyed" when Y has no planets or people
left, and "unsuccessfully attacked" when score ≤ 0. If the resource
`News.AttackVictim` (default 1) is 0, Y is not named: "a smaller empire"
when X has more planets and a higher net worth, "a larger empire" when
fewer of both, otherwise "another empire". Victory report `3b7a:023b` ("You have won the battle!
You capture N planets and N credits"; the WinWar screen 1 time in 5);
defeat: "You have lost the battle. You lost ...", LoseWar screen; a
defender with nothing left "is completely destroyed!!!"; the defender is
told "You defended against ...".

The defender's soldier and heavy-cruiser losses are shared with the
allies in proportion to what each put in (`3b7a:231b`..`27b0`;
`muldiv(a, b, c) = a * b / c`, `3b7a:00a9`, scales the operands down to
avoid overflow):

```
pool0 = defender.soldiers + drafted + sum(ally_soldiers)
lost  = (pool0 - remaining0) / 3
for each ally e: e.soldiers -= muldiv(lost, ally_soldiers[e], pool0)
defender.soldiers -= muldiv(lost, defender.soldiers, pool0)
# same for heavy cruisers with pool2 and ally_cruisers;
# RE-CHECK(logic): whether the drafted soldiers were added to
# defender.soldiers first (else their share of the losses is not charged)
if score < 0: each helping ally's army effectiveness -= 1 (min 0)
```

`RE-CHECK(logic)`: the effectiveness line (the sign test on the battle
score) is read, not tested.

## Permission check (`5c5b:0000`)

Before any attack: "You can not attack X because that empire is under
protection!" (target turn < 0); the treaty with the target is shown ("You
have a <treaty> with X"); a Neutrality/Peace Treaty forbids the attack;
allies cannot be attacked "unless you first break the treaty from the
Diplomacy Menu"; "That empire has collapsed!" when it has no planets or
population. Treaty kinds: see `docs/formats/empire.md` (`+0x0EC`).

### Treaty rules for attacks

```
t = target.treaty[attacker]                    # Empire +0x0EC + 4 * attacker
if t.kind == 1:  refuse  "Your Neutrality Treaty prevents you from attacking."
elif t.days > 0: refuse  "You cannot attack your allies unless you first
                          break the treaty from the Diplomacy Menu."
else:            ask     "Do you wish to continue"   # no treaty, or one run out
# then the attack limit check (508f:0000) and, if the attack goes ahead:
reset(target.treaty[attacker]); reset(attacker.treaty[target])
reset(e) = kind 0 (No Relations), days 0, defense percentages 0
           (the second entry also loses its pending status)
```

The reset is done by the permission check (`5c5b:02d1`) and again by
each attack (`3b7a:0884` invasion, `5c5b:060b` nuclear, `5c5b:0f19`
chemical, `5c5b:1862` psionic, `545d:0000` guerilla). Each copy is
followed by a block that sets the percentages for kinds 3..6, which
never fires because the kind was just set to 0 (dead code, harmless).
Covert operations reset the treaty with the target the same way, right
after paying (`409b:0508`), for insurgent aid, set-up (both empires
involved), dissension, demoralize, bombing and hostages; spying,
infiltration and bribing a spy leave it alone. The daily maintenance
(`5680:0c52`) and empire deletion (`6923:057d`) use the same reset when
a treaty runs out or an empire disappears.

So a treaty never survives an attack, and an ally must first break the
treaty (which takes effect at the partner's next turn, `diplomacy.md`)
and wait for it to be applied before attacking.

## Nuclear offensive (`5c5b:060b`)

Needs a bomb: bit 0 of Empire byte `+0x227` ("You have no nuclear
weapons!"); the Galactic Coordinator's warning is shown first. Using it:

```
attacker.flags_227 &= ~1;  attacker.attacks (+0x229) += 1
if galaxy.nuke_power (+0x3B2) > 50: galaxy.nuke_power -= 30
if galaxy.x3B4 > 3: galaxy.x3B4 -= 1

victim = attacker if rnd(33) == 0 else target     # "Your bomb was booby-trapped"
# destroy about min(planets, nuke_power) planets, spread over all types
k0 = 100 / galaxy.x3B4 + 1          # x3B4 read before its -1; 6 with the default 20
k = smallest k in [k0 .. 100) with victim.planets / k <= nuke_power
for each planet type t: victim.Planets[t].count -= count / k
```

So one bomb destroys at most `1/k0` of each planet type (a sixth with
the defaults), less when `nuke_power` is the limit. Reports
(`5c5b:0a66`..`0ee2`):

- Booby-trapped (the attacker is the victim): "Your bomb was
  booby-trapped, and you completely destroyed N of your own planets with
  the Nuclear Bomb!"; news "X was hit by X's own nuclear bomb!".
- Otherwise the bomb is **always traced**: the attacker's Coordinator
  favor is halved (`+0x1B0 /= 2`), the news says "Y was hit by a nuclear
  bomb traced to X.", the victim's report says "You lost N planets in a
  Nuclear Attack from X", the attacker sees "You completely destroyed N
  planets with the Nuclear Bomb!" and the NukeWar screen 1 time in 3.
## Chemical warfare (`5c5b:0f19`)

Needs bit 1 of `+0x227` ("You have no chemical weapons!"). Accepting the
Coordinator's warning sets the attacker's favor to 0. Then:

```
attacker.flags_227 &= ~2;  attacker.attacks += 1
if rnd(10) == 0 and target.agents > 0:          # sabotage
    attacker.population -= attacker.population / 2
    # "Your opponent sent N agents to sabotage your weapon. You kill N
    #  million of your own civilians!"
else:
    target.population -= target.population / 2   # "ChemWar" screen
```

## Psionic attack (`5c5b:1862`)

Needs bit 2 of `+0x227` ("You have no psionic bomb!"); no randomness:

```
attacker.flags_227 &= ~4;  attacker.attacks += 1
target.violence (+0x190) = 7                     # "UNDER COUP"
target.army_eff = 0
attacker.favor /= 2
```

## Guerilla ambush (`545d:0000`)

Soldiers only. The attacker sends `A` soldiers and sets a withdrawal
threshold ("Withdraw after loss of how many soldiers?"); `F = A - threshold`.
`D` = the defender's soldiers.

```
round = 0
while A > F and D > 0 and round < 78:            # "A battle to the death..."
    if rnd(min(A,30000)) < rnd(min(D,30000)): A -= D / 300 + 1
    if rnd(min(A,30000)) < rnd(min(A,30000)): A -= A / 500 + 1   # attrition
    if rnd(min(D,30000)) < rnd(min(A,30000)): D -= A / 100 + 1
    round += 1
result = (A > F) - (A < F) - (D > 0)             # > 0: attacker wins
# the "Guerilla" screen is shown 1 time in 13
```

The ambush favors the attacker (hits remove `A/100` against `D/300`).
`result` is 1 (win) or -2..0 (failure). Aftermath (`545d:0480`..`0e3b`):

```
attacker.soldiers -= min(A0 - A, attacker.soldiers)    # full losses
attacker.attacks += 1                                  # +0x229
defender.soldiers -= (D0 - D) / 3                      # a third, min 0
if result > 0:                                         # success, anonymous
    attacker.score += 10
    attacker.army_eff -= 10;  defender.army_eff -= 5   # clamped 0..100
    if defender.violence < 7 and rnd(2) == 0:
        violence_up(defender)                          # "Riots break out in
                                                       #  your opponent's empire"
    # attacker: "You have weakened the enemy without revealing your identity."
    # defender: "Someone attempted a secret guerilla invasion of your empire!
    #            You lost N soldiers defending."
else:                                                  # discovered
    attacker.army_eff += 2 * result                    # result <= 0
    attacker.score = max(attacker.score - (rnd(200) + 220 - 40 * result), 0)
    reset both treaty entries (as for every attack)
    # "Your immoral acts have been discovered and reported to Y."
    # news / defender: "X attempted a guerilla invasion of Y."
```

The second treaty reset sits on the failure path only, but the
permission check (`5c5b:02d1`) has already reset the treaty before the
ambush, so relations end either way; a success only keeps the attacker
anonymous in the reports. `RE-CHECK(logic)`: that the guerilla menu goes
through the permission check like the other attacks.

`RE-CHECK(logic)`: `rnd(n)` here is `rand() * n / 32768` with `n` capped
at 30000 (int16).

## Pirate raid (`5fdf:0297`)

Needs a score of at least 100,000 and to be out of protection
(`5fdf:0de6`; see `docs/formats/pirate.md`). The fleet: credits to spend,
soldiers, fighters, heavy cruisers ("Specify your attack fleet"). The
credits buy the raid's strength:

```
p = 1000 if credits > 500 * net_worth else max(2 * credits / net_worth, 200)
money -= credits
S = soldiers_sent + pirate.soldiers        # combined pools, fixed for the raid
F = fighters_sent + pirate.fighters
H = cruisers_sent + pirate.heavy_cruisers

round = 0
loop:
    if rnd(1100) < p and pirate.soldiers > 0: pirate.soldiers -= S/80 + 1
    if rnd(1300) < p and pirate.heavy    > 0: pirate.heavy    -= H/80 + 1
    if rnd(1200) < p and pirate.fighters > 0: pirate.fighters -= F/80 + 1
    if rnd(1200) < p and pirate.stations > 0: pirate.stations -= pirate.stations/80 + 1
    if rnd(500) < 80 and soldiers > 0: soldiers -= S/80 + 1   # pirates hit back
    if rnd(500) < 80 and cruisers > 0: cruisers -= H/80 + 1
    if rnd(500) < 80 and fighters > 0: fighters -= F/80 + 1
    round += 1
    stop if round > 25
    stop if each remaining unit type <= half of what was sent    # retreat
    stop if pirate soldiers, heavy cruisers and fighters are all 0  # won
    stop if soldiers + cruisers + fighters < (S + H + F) / 5
```

(pirate values clamped at 0). The attacker loses everything that fell in
the raid (not a third, unlike an invasion).

Outcome (`5fdf:0a96`..`0d78`): a score built like the invasion's, from
comparisons of what is left on each side for fighters, soldiers and
heavy cruisers, plus ±5 from a heavy-cruiser ×13 comparison; a score > 0
is a win ("RaidWar" screen 1 time in 13). Plunder (`5fdf:0d81`):

```
d = 3
if attacker.turn < 0:          d += 3
if attacker.score > 100000:    d += 2
if attacker.planets > 500:     d += 2
if attacker.net_worth > 100000: d += 4
d -= (score > 3) + (score > 6) + (score > 9)
d = max(d, 2)
for each planet type t:
    take = clamp(pirate.planets[t] / d, 0, 100)
    attacker.Planets[t].count += take;  pirate.planets[t] -= take
for soldiers, fighters, defense stations, heavy cruisers, carriers,
    generals, covert agents: attacker gets pirate.stock / d
```

`RE-CHECK(logic)`: food and credits are shown undivided in the plunder
list (`5fdf:0fea`, `11b5`); whether they are taken whole, and the exact
outcome score, are not fully traced.
"Spy on Pirates" (`5fdf:19d9`, attack menu choice 4) is free and only
shows a table, "Spy Report on Pirate Teams" (PirateSpy screen): one row
per existing team (pirate # `+0x20 > 0` and a non-empty name, at most 9,
counted by `4b5f:0bdf`) with its number, name (resource
`Pirate<n>.Name`, else the record's name; `4b5f:0c38`) in its color
(`Pirate<n>.Color`, else `+0x8F`; `4b5f:0ced`), its planets (sum of the
planet counts, `4b5f:01ed`) and its net worth (`4b5f:022f`, formula in
`events.md`). It does not show the units, and nothing is changed.

## Covert operations (step 14, `409b:0a6d`)

Menu: Send spy, Insurgent aid, Set up, Support dissension, Demoralize
troops, Bombing operations, Infiltration, Take hostages, Bribe spy.
Common preparation (`409b:084d`): check that the empire can pay the
operation's cost, choose the target (`409b:033d`), confirm, pay
(`money -= cost`) and log the operation in a history object at Empire
`+0x22F`. A caught agent is reported to the target ("A covert agent from
... was caught spying on your empire and was terminated!"). The operation
costs are not read yet.

### Success test (`409b:0197`)

Used by the operations that can fail (agents caught: "... was caught
spying on your empire and was terminated!"):

```
if me == target: success
a = my.agents     * (target.planets + 300)
d = target.agents * (my.planets + 300)
a, d = a + d / 5, d + a / 5          # both computed from the original values
while a > 32000 or d > 32000: a /= 2; d /= 2      # unsigned 16-bit after this
if a == 0: fail
if d == 0: success
success = a + rnd(d) > d + rnd(a)    # rnd(d) is drawn first
```

### Operations (code `409b:0e40`..`2849`)

What each one does, from its messages; the exact effects are not
transcribed yet (`RE-CHECK(logic)`):

| Operation | Cost | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Send spy | 3,100 (880 while protected) | shows the target's status ("Your spy was successful. Spy results are...") |
| Insurgent aid | 10,000 | on success the target's violence level rises (`1c59:0009`; "Your spy was successful in raising X's insurgency to <state>"; refused when it is already at the top) |
| Set up | 20,000 | delayed (below): makes one empire believe another attacked it |
| Support dissension | 25,000 | delayed (below) |
| Demoralize troops | 30,000 | delayed (below) |
| Bombing operations | 30,000 | on success: 2 in 3 the target loses **all** its food, otherwise half (`409b:1ceb`; "CovBomb" screen 1 in 8); on failure the agent may also blow himself up or be electrocuted |
| Infiltration | 30,000 | "Intercept Messages" (plants a spy that reports the target's messages) or "Diplomatic Status" (shows its treaties) |
| Take hostages | 50,000 | delayed (below) |
| Bribe spy | 50,000 | turns one of the target's agents ("You have successfully bribed an agent from ..."); needs the target to have agents and no spy of yours already there |

Costs are set at `409b:0a87`. Every operation runs the success test;
a failed operation costs the attacker one covert agent (`+0x22B` − 1) and
the target is told ("A covert agent from X was caught ... and was
terminated/executed!").

### Delayed effects (`4c47`, `CovertOp.II`)

Several operations do not act at once: they create a record (stream
format, `II.md`) in `CovertOp.II`, resolved later for the target. The
record classes found so far share `+0x02` target empire #, `+0x10` sender
empire #, `+0x12` success flag:

| Class | Resolved by | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Dissension | `4c47:052e` | success: target soldiers -= soldiers / (`rnd(7)` + 9) ("N soldiers dissented from your army due to propaganda"), the sender's agent comes back (+1); failure: the agent "was caught trying to support dissension and was executed!" |
| Demoralize | `4c47:0bf3` | success: target army effectiveness -= effectiveness / (`rnd(7)` + 7), clamped 0..100 ("Mysterious shipments of alcohol demoralized your troops."); the sender's agent comes back (+1) |
| Hostages | `4c47:1292` | success: ransom = money / (`rnd(3)` + 5) + bank / (`rnd(5)` + 7), taken from the target and paid to the sender ("Terrorists took hostages and you had to pay N credits as ransom."), money capped at 2,000,000,000 |
| Setup | `4c47:1bc9` | record: `+0x10` sender, `+0x14` framed "attacker", target = "defender". Success: the treaty between attacker and defender is cleared on both sides exactly as after a real attack (same bit-field updates as `3b7a:0884`), the attack is reported as if it happened (`3f61`), the sender's agent comes back. Failure: "Your covert agent was caught setting up ..." / the target learns "X was caught trying to make you think Y attacked you" |

Investments are in the same segment: a listing with Credits / Turn /
Hours (`4c47:29cb`) and a payout (`4c47:2c42`, "Your ... have returned
your investment" / "have crashed, giving you only N credits in the
bank") that credits the bank in chunks of 10,000,000 and 10,000 so it
never passes 2,000,000,000. They are bonds, fully described in
`bank.md` ("Investments (bonds)").

```

`docs/game/bank.md`:

```md
# Solar Bank (turn step 15)

`3e40:0000` (step 15 of `turn.md`; also reachable from the food market and
the expenses screen). Menu "Withdraw, take a Loan, Invest, Bonds,
Deposit, or Quit" (keys `QDWLBIS`, plus "See Investments"). In the
unregistered original the bank refuses entry ("You are not allowed to
visit the bank in the unregistered versions!"); the port has everything
unlocked (`DESIGN.md`). Partly transcribed, **not checked against the
game**: `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port.

The bank balance is Empire `+0x19C`; a negative balance is a loan, repaid
through the yearly bill (`expenses.md`). One rate serves both savings and
loans: Galaxy int16 `+0x3BE` (3 in the sample), shown as a "daily
interest rate" for deposits and an "annual interest rate" for loans.

Menu keys: **D** deposits (or, with a loan, repays), **W** withdraws
(only with savings), **L** takes a loan (only when the balance is ≤ 0),
**I** lists investments, **B** bonds (both `Investments` below).

```
# Deposit / repay ('D', 3e40:0761)
if bank >= 0:   max = min(money, 2,000,000,000 - bank)
                # "[SRE can only handle numbers up to ..., so some money
                #  will have to stay in the bank.]"
else:           max = money        # "You have loaned N credits at R%
                                   #  annual interest rate. How much do
                                   #  you wish to pay back?"
money -= amount; bank += amount    # paying more than the loan leaves savings

# Withdraw ('W', only when bank > 0, 3e40:09e3)
max = min(bank, 2,000,000,000 - money)
# moved in steps of 10,000,000 while money < 1,990,000,000, then of
# 10,000 while money < 2,000,000,000 (avoids overflow); same result.

# Loan ('L', only when bank <= 0, 3e40:0c8a)
limit = turns_played * 35                           # Empire +0x194
      + soldiers * 3 + fighters * 8 + stations * 10
      + heavy_cruisers * 10 + generals * 13 + food / 31
      + 230 * (n[E] + n[T] + n[U]) + 500 * (n[O] + n[F])
      + 400 * n[S] + 330 * n[G] + 50 * n[R] + 1100 * n[A]
      + 150,000                                      # 3e40:00f0..02d5
available = limit + bank                             # bank <= 0 here
if available <= 0: "Your credit is overdrawn."
if planets + 8 * n[P] < 100 * n[A]:                  # "This bank rewards
    available += available / 2                       #  environmentalists ..."
# "At a R% annual interest rate, how much do you wish to borrow?" MAX=available
finance_charge = amount / 100 * rate                 # "That will require a N finance charge"
yearly_payment = amount / 70 * rate + 1              # "The yearly payment is N"
# "Are you sure you want a loan"
bank  -= amount + finance_charge                     # the charge is added to the debt
money += amount
Empire[+0x1A4] += yearly_payment                     # billed by expenses.md
```

If the loan would push money past 2,000,000,000 ("The bank is unable to
find the full sum of money for loan."), it is paid out in steps of
10,000,000 (debt + 10,000,000 + 100,000 × rate each) while money <
1,990,000,000, then of 10,000 (debt + 10,000 + 100 × rate each) until money
reaches 2,000,000,000 or the amount is used up. That path skips the
`+0x1A4` update (`3e40:1116` jumps past it), so a capped loan adds no
yearly payment: a bug of the original (`original-bugs.md`).

## Interest (every turn, turn step 3, `48cb:2598`)

```
if -500,000,000 <= bank < 0:          # loan: the debt grows
    bank += bank / 100 * rate
if 0 < bank <= 1,000,000,000:         # savings
    bank += bank / 500 * rate
```

So with the default 3 %, savings earn 0.6 % per turn and a loan costs 3 %
per turn, on top of the yearly repayment billed by the expenses step.

`RE-CHECK(formula)`: all of the above is read from the disassembly, not
yet checked against a game; planet letters as in `empire.md`
(`PETFROGUSA`).

## Investments (bonds)

"Investments" are bonds: there is **no growth or crash of value over
time**. A bond pays a fixed amount at maturity; it "crashes" only when
its issuer cannot pay. Menu `1719:10b8`: List investments, Make an
investment, Configure your bonds, Kancel bond offers.

### The bond record (stream object, `0x6A` bytes, class `4c47:2773`)

| Offset | Content |
|---|---|
| `+0x02` | holder empire # (-1 once the holder is gone) |
| `+0x0C` | due time (time_t; "Hours" column = `(due - now + 1800) / 3600`) |
| `+0x10` | amount to pay at maturity (money) |
| `+0x18` | bond name, e.g. "Galactic Treasury Bonds" |
| `+0x66` | holder's turn counter (`+0x194`) at which it matures |
| `+0x68` | issuer empire #, -1 = Galactic Treasury |

A bond is due when the time is reached **and** the holder's turn counter
`>= +0x66` (`4c47:298d`, "whichever is later"). Due bonds are processed
at turn step 5 (`4c47:32f1`, which walks the whole timed-record queue
`Data/CovertOp`, shared with the delayed covert operations).

### Galactic Treasury Bonds (`1719:000a`)

```
price = 8500, payout = 10000, issuer = -1, due after 1 real hour
max   = min(money / 8500, 200000)
# maturity turns: count half-steps of the bank rate from 8.5M to 10M
x = 8_500_000; n = 0
while n < 200 and x < 10_000_000:
    x += x / (turns_per_day * 100) * bank_rate    # Galaxy +0x39E, +0x3BE
    n += 1
turns = max(n / 2, 5)
```

With the defaults (rate 3, 5 turns per day) `n = 28`, so 14 turns. The
price is subtracted from money.

### Player bonds (`1719:0b7d` configure, `1719:0394` buy)

An empire can offer its own bonds (Empire fields `+0x2A3..+0x2D1`,
`empire.md`). Defaults when first configured: price 8,500, payout 10,000,
10 turns, 1 hour, at most 1 outstanding. Limits: price ≤ 1,000,000,
payout ≤ 2,000,000, turns ≤ 100, hours ≤ 240, maximum outstanding
≤ 1000, and turns and hours cannot both be 0. The Galactic Coordinator
refuses a bond that is "too profitable":

```
reject if (payout - price) / (3 * turns + hours) * 30 > price    # 1719:0f58
```

The buy menu lists the Treasury and every other empire whose offer has a
price and fewer outstanding bonds than its maximum. Buying `n`:

- `n <= min(money / price, max_outstanding - outstanding)`;
- the issuer receives `n * price` into money, the overflow above the
  2,000,000,000 cap into the bank; if the bank overflows too, `n` is cut
  by the excess (rounded up to whole bonds): "Your financial team could
  only acquire N bonds at this time.";
- the buyer pays `n * price` from money; the issuer's outstanding count
  (`+0x2C3`) grows by `n`; maturity = buyer's turns + issuer turns, and
  issuer hours.

### Maturity (`4c47:2c42`) and the issuer's payment (`4c47:3bc9`)

1. The issuer pays (Treasury: always in full). An empire pays from money,
   then the bank; if still short it sells assets at **one third of their
   buy price**, repeated round by round while something is left to sell:
   100 soldiers, 100 fighters, 100 defense stations, 10 generals, 100
   heavy cruisers, 10 carriers, 10 covert agents, 100 food (for 200), 10
   population (for 100), then one planet of each type; only stocks above
   the chunk size are sold. The issuer is told "N credits were taken from
   you to pay for bond payoffs. Some of your assets had to be sold ...".
2. The holder is credited the full payout into the bank, then money,
   never above 2,000,000,000 each; the rest is kept in the record ("N
   credits have been re-invested because your bank was full.") and paid
   on a later turn.
3. Message: payout fully paid: "Your <bonds> have returned your
   investment, giving you N credits in the bank"; partly paid: "have
   crashed, giving you only N" (the unpaid part is taken back); nothing
   (issuer deleted, `4c47:284e` zeroes the payout): "have crashed!".
4. When the record is fully paid, the issuer's outstanding count drops
   by one.

`RE-CHECK(logic)`: the round-by-round sale order and the exact
overflow handling are read from the disassembly, not tested.

# Buying and selling (turn step 16)

`1af6:07dd` (step 16 of `turn.md`) is the "Government Spending" screen
("Buying" / "Selling", columns Item, Price, Owned; "Release Planets").
Prices come from nine functions in segment `1af6` (resident code),
listed in menu order. The **sell price is the buy price / 3** for every
item (`1af6:08f1`). Transcribed from the disassembly, **not yet checked
against the game's screen**: `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port.

Notation: `nw` = net worth (`1c59:028b`, see `docs/formats/empire.md`),
`planets` = total planets, `turn` = Empire `+0x194` (negative while in
protection, so prices are lower then), `score` = `+0x174`. All int32,
divisions truncate toward zero. The **inflation** setting (Galaxy
`+0x384`, asked at reset) selects the formula.

| Item | Function | Without inflation | With inflation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Soldiers | `1af6:0006` | 180 + nw/1000 | 180 + 2·turn + soldiers/1800 + fighters/12400 + nw/5000 |
| Fighters | `1af6:00b8` | 240 + nw/800 | 240 + (5·turn)/2 + soldiers/7000 + fighters/1690 + nw/400 |
| Defense stations | `1af6:0172` | 320 + nw/700 | 320 + 3·turn + soldiers/7500 + fighters/9000 + stations/1460 + nw/300 |
| Generals | `1af6:024c` | 670 + nw/300 | 670 + 14·turn + soldiers/1790 + generals/170 + planets/10 |
| Command ship | `1af6:0307` | 8800 + nw/100 | 5000 + soldiers/850 + fighters/950 |
| Colonize planets | `1af6:0379` | 13000 + planets + nw/100 | see below |
| Covert agents | `1af6:0495` | 4300 + nw/200 | 2218 + 18·turn + agents + 7·planets + score/10 |
| Heavy cruisers | `1af6:0542` | 1100 + nw/600 | 1100 + 7·turn + fighters/1220 + planets/5 + stations/2500 + nw/150 |
| Carriers | `1af6:0624` | 850 + nw/700 | 850 + 7·turn + planets/10 + nw/100 |

`(5·turn)/2` truncates toward zero (computed as `(x - sign) >> 1`).

Colonizing a planet with inflation:

```
d = 3 if turn < 0 (protection) else 2 if planets < 300 else 1
price = ((planets + score/2 + nw/10 + max(turn, 0)) * 97 + 50000) / d / 10
```

## Buying and selling a quantity (`61a6:010a`, `61a6:04d2`)

```
# buy ("Buy how many <item>?", MAX shown)
max = min(money / price, limit)          # limit: per item, -1 = none
if limit == 0: "No <item> are available to buy this year."
elif max == 0: "You can not afford any <item>!"
money -= n * price; owned += n

# sell ("Sell how many <item>?")
max = min(owned, (2,000,000,000 - money) / sell_price)   # sell_price = price / 3
money += n * sell_price; owned -= n
```

Military purchases can be turned off with the resource
`Spending.Military` (forcing supply-planet production). "Release
Planets" (`61a6:091b`) gives planets back to the Galaxy market and
lowers `+0x192`. `RE-CHECK(logic)`: which limit applies to each item.

## Colonizing planets (`61a6:0b7f`)

"Buy Planets": "There are N planets available" (Galaxy `+0x392`), "You
may buy N planets per turn" (Galaxy `+0x38E`, -1 = unlimited). Buying `N`
planets of a type (`61a6:071e`):

```
available -= N                      # the planets-in-market counter passed in
score += N * 3                      # verified on the turn5 -> turn6 sample
money -= N * price                  # money class 28ec:0199
```

The screen also reports pollution and food production per year
(`61a6:0eec`, `0f39`). `RE-CHECK(logic)`: how the per-turn limit is
counted, and which planet types can be bought.

## Command ship (`61a6:0384`, `48cb:2488`)

Empire int8 `+0x171` is the command ship's completion, 0..100 %. Buying it
on the spending screen (price from `1af6:0307`):

```
if ship >= 100: "You have already completed work on your command ship!"
elif money < price: "You can't afford to start your command ship now."
else:
    ship = 5 if ship == 0 else ship + 5      # "You added some strength ..."
    money -= price
```

Once started it builds itself every turn (turn step 2):

```
if ship > 0: ship += 5 if ship < 90 else 3 if ship < 95 else 1
ship = clamp(ship, 0, 100)
```

Its value counts in net worth and in the battle hit chance
(`attacks.md`, `ship / 2 + 50` out of 200).

# Civil war, riots and the Coordinator's aid (turn steps 24-25)

Transcribed from the disassembly, **not yet checked against a sample**
(except the insurgent riots, verified in issue #1): every other formula is
`RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in
`production.md`.

## Coordinator favor (step 24, `48cb:2731`)

Empire int32 `+0x1B0` is the Galactic Coordinator's favor toward the
empire. Each turn:

```
if favor < 0: favor += 1
if favor > 0: favor -= 2
if (planets - n[P]) / 10 < n[A]: favor += 1     # enough anti-pollution
```

Favor pays for the Coordinator's recovery aid below; using nuclear or
chemical weapons "seriously angers It" (attack code, not yet read).

## Coordinator's allowance (session start, `48cb:232d`)

Paid by `1e7b:0f61`, once per play session before the turn loop
("You receive N credits from the Galactic Coordinator!"):

```
if turn (+0x194) >= next_allowance (+0x19A):
    divisor = 400 if turn < -25 else 300 if turn < 1 else 100
    amount = max(coordinator_treasury (Galaxy +0x3AC) / divisor, 0)
    money += amount;  coordinator_treasury -= amount
    next_allowance = turn + turns_per_interval (Galaxy +0x39E)
```

So an empire gets it at most once per day's worth of turns, and
protected empires (turn < 1) get a third of what established ones get.
Verified exactly (issue #9, `verification.md`): a new empire at turn -20
got 9980 / 300 = 33 and `+0x19A` went from -20 to -15; the other
empire, at turn -16 with `+0x19A` = -15, got nothing.

## Civil war (step 25, `44e1:07cc`)

Two kinds, flagged in Empire byte `+0x1C4` by earlier turn steps: bit 0
by unpaid planets (`expenses.md`), bit 1 by starving people (`food.md`). `violence_up()` is `1c59:0009`
(violence level + 1, max 7).

```
if flags(+0x1C4) & 1:                         # planned civil war
    violence_up()
    lost = 0
    for t in 0..9:
        loss = min(plan[t], Planets[t].count)  # plan = int32[10] at +0x1C7
        galaxy.planets_in_market += loss
        Planets[t].count -= loss;  lost += loss
    pct = lost * 100 / planets                 # planets after the loss
    killed = pop * pct / 100;  pop -= killed
    lose_military(pct)
    size = "minor" if pct < 20 else "small" if pct < 30 else
           "large" if pct < 50 else "major" if pct < 70 else (string 0x2076)

elif flags(+0x1C4) & 2:                       # insurgents (riots), verified
    pct = clamp(int32(+0x223) * 100 / pop, 0, 30)   # pop after step 22
    pop -= pop * pct / 100
    violence_up()
    for t in 0..9:
        loss = Planets[t].count * pct / 100
        galaxy.planets_in_market += loss;  Planets[t].count -= loss
    lose_military(pct)
    size by pct: < 10 "inconsequential", < 20, else (strings 0x209A, 0x20AA, 0x20B0)

lose_military(pct) (44e1:04f2): each of soldiers, fighters, defense
stations, heavy cruisers, generals, carriers and light cruisers loses
unit * pct / 100, rounded down (verified: 106 heavy cruisers at 4 % lose 4).
```

Reports: "Your people are in riots due to ...", "N million people were
killed in the riots.", "..., your empire plunges into a ... CIVIL WAR!",
"You lose N planets (total ...)", "You also lose ...", "... but your
officials prevent a civil war from breaking out." An option "Display hints
to avoid civil wars" explains the causes (tourism vs. ore, pollution from
petroleum, food, loans).

## Coordinator aid (end of `44e1:07cc`)

Offered ("The Galactic Coordinator offers to give you some funds to
recover from ...", "Do you accept") when all hold:

```
favor >= 25 and pct > 25
and money + bank < 100,000,000
and soldiers + fighters + defense_stations + cruisers + agents < 2000
and planets < 300
```

If accepted: `favor -= 25`; `money += min(old_favor, 100) * planets * 15`
("You receive N credits", "The Galactic Coordinator wishes you luck in
rebuilding your empire!").
