`docs/game/diplomacy.md`:

```md
# Diplomacy (treaties)

Segment `70d1`. Menu "Diplomacy" (`70d1:0000`): View Relations, Propose
Other Treaty, Break Treaty. Treaty kinds and the 4-byte treaty entry are
in `docs/formats/empire.md` (`+0x0EC`). Partly transcribed:
`RE-CHECK(logic)` in the port.

## Proposing (`70d1:03bd`, `70d1:0a10`)

- Pick an empire and a treaty kind (names from the resources
  `Treaty.Neutrality`, `Treaty.FreeTrade`, `Treaty.MinorAlliance`,
  `Treaty.ArmedDefense`, `Treaty.CruiserDefense`, `Treaty.TotalDefense`,
  `Treaty.Custom`, `Treaty.Break`; `70d1:2932`).
- Duration: "How many days?", 1..14. It becomes the treaty's byte 0,
  which the daily maintenance counts down (`maintenance.md`).
- Defense percentages ("This treaty will provide N% soldier defense and
  N% cruiser defense"): Minor Alliance 20/20, Armed Defense 60/0, Cruiser
  Protection 0/60, Total Defense 40/40. A Custom Treaty asks for both
  ("The total percentage of cruisers and soldiers can be up to 60%").
- Defense treaties are refused with the current Weapons Master, on
  either side ("You cannot get a defense treaty while you are the Weapons
  Master!", "X is the Weapons Master; you cannot get a defense treaty with
  today's Weapons Master").
- Only one pending action per pair of empires (below).

## Answering (`70d1:1ddf`, at the start of the partner's turn)

"X proposes a <treaty> for N days. It involves N% soldier defense and N%
cruiser defense. Do you accept" → "Treaty Accepted" / "Treaty Rejected";
the proposer is told "X accepts / rejects the <treaty> proposal". If the
receiver is the Weapons Master, an accepted defense treaty becomes a
Neutrality treaty ("Because you are the Weapons Master, the treaty has
been changed to Neutrality.").

## Breaking (`70d1:1139`)

"You send word that you wish to break the treaty." The break is applied
when the partner next plays: "X has dishonorably broken a treaty with
you!" (`70d1:1e6e`). Breaking is needed before attacking an ally
(`attacks.md`). "View Relations" (`70d1:17b1`) lists every treaty.

## Where proposals and breaks are stored

Verified for a proposal and its acceptance (issue #5, `verification.md`).

Nowhere else than the treaty entries themselves: there is no file for
them. Each pair of empires has two entries, `A.treaty[B]` and
`B.treaty[A]` (Empire `+0xEC + 4 × other`, `empire.md`), and bits 13..17
hold the pending action:

| Status | Label | Set by | Handled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | | |
| 1 | Proposed | A proposes to B (`70d1:0a10`): written into **B's** entry for A, with the proposed kind, days and percentages | B's next turn (`70d1:1ddf`): "A proposes a ..." |
| 2 | Rejected | B rejects (`70d1:25b5`) | A's next turn: "B rejects the ... proposal", then cleared |
| 3 | Accepted | B accepts (`70d1:2463`); both entries get the new treaty, status 3 in **A's** entry for B, 0 in B's | A's next turn: "B accepts the <treaty> (S%/C%).", then cleared |
| 4 | Treaty Broken | A breaks (`70d1:1139`, "You send word ...") | B's next turn (`70d1:1e65`): "A has (dishonorably) broken a treaty with you!"; the kind is reset to 0 and the defense percentages to that kind's values |

Consequences:

- One pending action per pair: proposing again over a status 1 asks
  "You have already proposed a <kind> for N turns to X ... Replace
  previous actions"; a break already sent says "You have already sent
  word that you wish to break the treaty!", and proposing over it
  cancels it.
- After rejecting A's proposal, proposing to A first asks "You just
  rejected A's treaty. Do you wish to send a new treaty instead".
- Proposing the treaty already in force says "You already have a ...".
- Breaking has **no penalty** besides the message: no score, Coordinator
  favor or trade effect is applied (`70d1:1e40..2009`).

`RE-CHECK(logic)`: which side keeps the old treaty while a proposal is
pending (the proposal overwrites B's entry; A's entry still has the
treaty in force) and how a rejection restores B's entry (`70d1:26dd`
copies it back from A's side) are read, not tested.

# Trading (segment `6e3e`)

Player-to-player trade deals, enabled by the resource `Trading`
(default 1; turn step 18). Deals travel as stream records in `Trading.II`
and expire after the resource `Trade.Expire` (default 4).

## The deal record (`6e3e:04b0`, `0x52` bytes in a `0x56` wrapper)

| Offset | Content |
|---|---|
| `+0x08` / `+0x0A` | empire the record is addressed to / the other side (swapped each time the record travels back) |
| `+0x0C` | status: 1 pending at the receiver, 2 accepted, 4 rejected or refused, 0 void (an empire is gone, `6e3e:0088`) |
| `+0x0E` | **offer**: goods block (below) |
| `+0x2E` | **demand**: goods block |
| `+0x3C` | expiry, from `Trade.Expire` |
| `+0x44`, `+0x46` | -1 at creation |

Goods block (`0x20` bytes, `6e3e:0152`; item tables `DS:aa36` = Empire
field, `DS:aa4a` = block offset, both stored + 1):

| Block | Item | Empire field |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x00` | soldiers | `+0x154` |
| `+0x04` | fighters | `+0x158` |
| `+0x08` | heavy cruisers | `+0x160` |
| `+0x0C` | generals | `+0x168` |
| `+0x10` | carriers | `+0x164` |
| `+0x14` | credits | money `+0x17C` |
| `+0x18` | food | `+0x18C` |
| `+0x1C` | covert agents | `+0x22B` |

## Formulas

```
# carriers needed for one block (6e3e:03da); heavy cruisers and credits
# need none, carriers in the block carry themselves
carriers(g) = max(0, ceil((g.fighters + g.generals + 3 * g.agents) / 150)
                   + ceil(g.soldiers / 500) + ceil(g.food / 10000)
                   - g.carriers)
fleet = max(carriers(offer), carriers(demand))        # 6e3e:05fe
# "Current fleet requires N carriers." / "This is N more carriers than
#  you have." / "You don't have enough carriers to send the fleet."

# value of a block (6e3e:01c5): goods in transit, Empire +0x16C
value(g) = g.credits / 100000 + 7 * g.agents + g.soldiers + g.fighters
         + 3 * g.heavy_cruisers + 3 * g.carriers + 2 * g.generals
```

`+0x16C` counts in the net worth at half value, so goods in transit
still count for their owner.

## Life of a deal

1. **Send** (`6e3e:108f`, "Send this trade deal", optional message,
   "Trading fleet sent."): the offered goods and credits leave the
   sender at once; `sender[+0x16C] += value(offer)`.
2. **Receive** (turn step 4, `6e3e:1f14` → accept code `6e3e:13c4`):
   "X has sent a trading deal: ... In return for ..., you must send back
   ...". Automatic refusals (status 4): the receiver is in protection
   ("since you are in protection, you cannot trade with other empires"),
   or the two empires have no treaty at all (kind 0: "you no longer have
   any relations with that empire"). If the receiver cannot pay
   (`6e3e:1290`: for every item `demand - offer <= owned`, credits
   included), it may only keep the deal for later or reject it.
   - **Accept**: for every item `owned += offer - demand`; credits
     `money += offer - demand`, the part above 2,000,000,000 into the
     bank; `receiver[+0x16C] += value(demand) - value(offer)` while the
     demanded goods travel; status 2, record sent back.
     **Observed instead** (issue #7, value(demand) = 0): the receiver's
     `+0x16C` stayed 0 and the **sender's** fell from 400 to 0 at the
     acceptance, not on the sender's next turn. `RE-CHECK(logic)`: the port
     moves the sender's value at acceptance; which formula applies when
     both sides have a value is not tested.
   - **Reject**: status 4, record sent back.
   - **Ignore for now / Keep for later**: stays pending (status 1).
3. **Back at the sender** (`6e3e:1b9a`): the goods in the record are
   added (accepted: the demanded goods; rejected or expired: the offer
   comes back), credits to money then bank, and `+0x16C -= value`.

Verified for an accepted deal (issue #7, `verification.md`): the carrier
count, the offer leaving at once, the receiver's stocks and the credits
reaching the sender on its next turn. `RE-CHECK(logic)`: rejected and
expired deals are read from the code, not tested.

```

```md
# Research, overpopulation and weapon traders (turn step 9)

`6571:2459` (step 9 of `turn.md`). Transcribed from the disassembly,
**not checked against the game**: `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port.
Notation as in `production.md`.

## Order

```
if any pirate team is active (4b5f:0bdf > 0):
    p = pick a pirate (6571:230c)
    random_events(p)                      # 6571:00ac, see below
if rnd(3) == 0: research()
else:           mothership()

```
## Research (`RESEARCH.DAT`)

`DATA/RESEARCH.DAT` holds 41 records of 255 bytes (read by segment
`6db2`):

| Offset | Type | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | int16 | record number |
| 0x02 | int32 | cost per planet, in research points |
| 0x06 | int16 | planet type 0..9 (`PETFROGUSA`; e.g. 5 = Ore) |
| 0x08 | int16 | mode: 1 = raise base production, 2 = raise current production |
| 0x0A | int32 | amount |
| 0x0E | char[] | message, with `^\x` color codes (e.g. "New mining techniques increase ore production!") |

```
r = record rnd(count)                          # count from 6db2:05da
if r.type not in 0..9: error "R.index( ... ) in random() is ..."
cost = Planets[r.type].count * r.cost
if cost <= research_points (+0x293) and Planets[r.type].count > 0
   and rnd(2) == 0:
    Planets[r.type].base    (+0x4) += r.amount if r.mode == 1 else 0
    Planets[r.type].current (+0x8) += r.amount if r.mode == 2 else 0
    research_points -= cost
    show r.message
```

## Mothership

```
if research_points >= 10000 and not (flags_227 & 8):
    flags_227 |= 8      # "Your research planets develop a Mothership carrier ..."
```

## Overpopulation of agents and generals

Government planets house generals and covert agents (`48cb:27c6`):

```
room = n[G] * 300 - generals * 6 - agents      # 50 generals per government planet
excess_agents   = clamp(-room,     0, agents)
excess_generals = clamp(-room / 6, 0, generals)    # 48cb:282f
agents   -= excess_agents / 3     # "covert agents are killed in covert civil wars
                                  #  caused by spy overpopulation"
generals -= excess_generals / 3   # "generals kill each other in military
                                  #  conflicts caused by overpopulation of generals"
```

`RE-CHECK(formula)`: the exact threshold before killing (the code tests
`excess >= 2`) and the rounding.

## Weapon traders

Only in registered games in the original (`System +0x128`); the port is
always registered. One check per weapon, in this order:

```
for weapon, bit, resource in (nuclear, 1, Attacks.Nuclear),
                             (chemical, 2, Attacks.Chemical),
                             (psionic, 4, psionic resource at DS:8182):
    if resource enabled and agents / (planets + 200) > rnd(20)
       and not (flags_227 & bit) and turn > 0:
        offer it                  # trader name picked with rnd(5) for the bomb
```

| Weapon | Offer | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Nuclear bomb | "You are approached by a sleazy trader / Bauk'ar de Gorash / Torras Ysarr / a well dressed trader / Diku Mudd who offers you a Nuclear Bomb" | 3,000,000 |
| Chemicals | "A well-dressed trader approaches you and offers to sell a megaton of Chemicals for chemical warfare" | 1,000,000 |
| Psionic bomb | "A well-known smuggler approaches you and offers to sell a one-pound Psionic Bomb" | Galaxy `+0x3C2` (10,000,000 after reset) |

Buying sets the weapon's bit in Empire `+0x227` ("You have bought one
nuclear bomb from the underground trading market"); payment is taken
from money and the rest from the bank ("But you can't afford it" when
both are short). After a psionic bomb is sold, its price becomes
`price * 3 + 1,000,000`; the daily maintenance lowers it to 75 % per day,
never below 5,000,000.

## Random events (`6571:00ac`)

Run with one active pirate team `p`, chosen at random weighted by Pirate
int16 `+0xD4` (`6571:230c`). Each event below is an independent check, in
this order. Many move what is lost to the pirate team (the pirate's
credits `+0x90`, food `+0x94`, soldiers `+0x98`, heavy cruisers `+0xA4`,
generals `+0xAC`, agents `+0xB0`, planets by type `+0xB4..+0xC6`).
Triggers are transcribed (note `<=`: e.g. `rnd(1000) <= 30` is a 31/1000
chance). All effect sizes are exact (read from the code; not yet checked against
a game). They will not be tested in the original: inexact random
events are accepted in the port (decision on issue #4). `turn > 0` = out of protection.

| # | Event | Trigger | Effect (sketch) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Planets revolt "under the leadership of" a random leader (Amit Patel, Emperor Reko, Bill Clinton, Gengher Kahn, King Jello, a Talking Horse, Ziggy the Dinosaur; `rnd(40)` table) | turns used today = turns per day / 2, `turn > 0`, and the empire is the Planet Master or `planets / 100 > pirate planets` (`4b5f:01ed`) | per type: `c = min(count, 300)`, `m = min(c * (tax / 10) / 100, 20)`, `revolt = clamp(rnd(m), 0, count - 1)`; revolting planets join the pirate (`+0xB4 + 2t`); "Revolt" screen 1 in 5 |
| — | **Gate for events 2..18** | `net_worth > pirate_net_worth / 20` (`4b5f:022f`), otherwise no further event this turn | |
| 2 | Thieves: "N credits were stolen by <pirate>" | `rnd(5) == 0`, planets > 60, `turn > 0` | `stolen = rnd(100) * (money / 10000)`, to the pirate's credits; "Thieves" screen 1 in 15 |
| 3 | "N cruisers were stolen by <pirate>" | `rnd(45) == 0`, net worth > 10,000, `turn > 0` | `stolen = cruisers * rnd(10) / 100`, applied only if `stolen <= cruisers / 5`; to the pirate's heavy cruisers |
| 4 | "N cruisers were given to you by Aunt Edna!" | `rnd(45) == 0`, net worth < 100,000 | heavy cruisers += `rnd(planets * 10)` |
| 5 | "N million people were killed in riots due to high tax rates!", "Violence increases in your empire!" | `tax * tax > rnd(8000)` (about 6.6 % at 23 % tax), population > 500, planets > 0 | `killed = rnd(tax) * (pop / 200)`; with `r = score * 3 / planets`: halve if `r > 100`, then −1/5 if `r > 50`, −1/11 if `r > 10`, −1/17 if `r > 1`; violence + 1 (if < 7), + 1 more on `rnd(3) == 0` and on `rnd(7) == 0`; "HighTax" screen 1 in 15 |
| 6 | Food lost: eaten by velociraptors / destroyed by crop disease / swallowed by Arcadian locusts / eaten by the Sysop (local play), or stolen by <pirate> | `rnd(30) == 0`, planets > 30, `turn > 0` | `loss = rnd(100) * (food / 700)`; then `rnd(10)`: 0..4 = destroyed by a creature (jump table `6571:0e4f`), 5..9 = goes to the pirate's food ("FoodLost" screen 1 in 15) |
| 8 | "N megatons of food were destroyed due to harsh weather." | `rnd(1000) <= 50`, food planets ≥ 100, `turn > 0` | `loss = food_planets * (rnd(5000) / 3)`; applied only if the stock is at least `loss` |
| 9 | "You received N megatons of potatoes and onions / carrots and peas / leafy vegetables / candy bars / cheese for your birthday." (`rnd(5)` picks the food) | `rnd(1000) <= 30` | food += `rnd(5000)` |
| 10 | "N exatons of toxic fumes were released due to a pumping accident." | `rnd(1000) <= 30`, petroleum planets ≥ 10, `turn > 0` | pollution += `rnd(petroleum planets) / 3` |
| 11 | "... released when one of your advisors burped" | `rnd(1000) <= 10`, petroleum planets ≥ 100, `turn > 0` | pollution += `rnd(petroleum planets) / 10` |
| 12 | "N soldiers desert your training camps." | `rnd(1000) <= 50`, supply planets ≥ 5, `turn > 0` | `lost = min(rnd(25) * (supply_planets / 3), soldiers)`; to the pirate's soldiers |
| 13 | "N soldiers joined your army." | `rnd(1000) <= 10` | soldiers += `planets * 5` (no random part) |
| 14 | "A general was captured by <pirate>" | `rnd(1000) <= 50`, generals ≥ 50, `turn > 0` | generals − 1, pirate generals + 1 |
| 15 | "A general lost a game of Solar Hangman, and was hanged." | `rnd(1000) <= 10`, generals ≥ 50, `turn > 0` | generals − 1 |
| 16 | "A general was lost bungee-jumping off the cliffs of Raekel IV." | `rnd(1000) <= 10`, generals ≥ 50, `turn > 0` | generals − 1 |
| 17 | "N covert agents were captured by <pirate>" | `rnd(1000) <= 30`, agents ≥ 500, `turn > 0` | `lost = rnd(min(agents, 3000) / 20)` (200 when agents > 3000); to the pirate's agents |
| 18 | "N soldiers have been forced to join the <pirate> force." | `rnd(1000) <= 50`, soldiers ≥ 1000, `turn > 0` | `lost = rnd(soldiers / 20)`; to the pirate's soldiers |

The "Sysop" eater depends on `DS:beea` (remote session) and prints the
sysop name from System `+0x00`. Pirate planets and net worth used by the
triggers: `4b5f:01ed` = sum of the pirate's planets; `4b5f:022f` =
planets × 10 + credits / 100000 + agents × 7 + soldiers + fighters +
food / 10000 + heavy cruisers × 3 + defense stations × 2 + carriers × 2 +
generals × 5.
```

`docs/game/expenses.md`:

```md
# Expenses (turn step 11)

`5e47:0b9f` (step 11 of `turn.md`) shows the yearly bill "Your empire
requires N credits this year. You have M", offers "Pay everything
automatically" or a visit to the bank, then asks for each line (payment
input in `5e47:09e3`, "You must pay at least ..."). The amounts come from
`5e47:0000`, which fills a 0x18-byte bill. Applying the payments
(`5e47:03f6`) is below; its consequences land in later turn steps
("Not paying for maintenance of your empire may lead to DISASTEROUS
consequences").

Transcribed from the disassembly, **not yet checked against a sample**:
every formula is `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in
`production.md`; `planets` = total planet count (`1c59:004b`), `state` =
Empire `+0x190`.

## Bill (`5e47:0000`)

Listed in the order the bill presents them.

```
# +0x10  "Maintaining your planets requires"
if not inflation (Galaxy +0x384 == 0):
    f = -1400
    v = planets + 500
    while v >= 8: f += 800; v = v / 8
    f += LOG8[v]                    # v in 0..7
    planets_cost = planets * f      # ~ planets * (800*log8(planets+500) - 1400)
else:
    planets_cost = planets * (turn + 1000)       # turn = Empire +0x194
planets_cost = max(planets_cost, 0)

LOG8 = [0, 86, 266, 422, 533, 619, 689, 748]   # table at 5e47:03c6
# 800*log8(v) rounded down for v = 2..7; v = 1 gives 86, not 0 (keep it).

# +0x0C  "For your loan, the bank requires that you pay back"
loan_payment = 0
if bank < 0:                                    # a negative bank balance is a loan
    loan_payment = Empire int32 +0x1A4
    if loan_payment + bank > 0: loan_payment = -bank

# +0x00  "Your military requires"
military = soldiers*2 + fighters*4 + cruisers*12 + light_cruisers*10
         + defense_stations*5

# +0x08  "Violence within your empire can be reduced by spending"
violence = (planets + population*2) * ((state + 1) / 2)

# +0x04  "Your Army's effectiveness can be raised by spending"
upkeep = (fighters*30 + soldiers*15 + generals*75 + cruisers*50
          + light_cruisers*30) / 10 + 17
gap = min(100 - army_effectiveness, 20)         # Empire int8 +0x170, 0..100
effectiveness = upkeep / 100 * gap               # verified (issue #11): 715 / 100 * 19 = 133

# +0x14  "The Galactic Coordinator asks that you donate"
donation = taxable (Empire +0x1BC) * galactic_tax_rate (Galaxy +0x3B0)
if coordinator_treasury (Galaxy +0x3AC) > 1,500,000,000: donation = 0
```

Since `taxable` is the turn's income divided by 1000 (`production.md`),
the donation is the tax rate "per 1000 credits" asked at reset.

## Paying the bill (`5e47:03f6`)

Called with the bill and `paid`, a struct of the same layout holding what
the player chose to pay for each line. Lines are processed in this order:

```
# military (+0x00)
if paid.military < bill.military:
    short = (paid.military - bill.military) / (bill.military / 100 + 1)  # <= 0, percent
    int8 +0x1C5 = short
    int8 +0x1C6 = army_effectiveness + short
    flags(+0x1C4) |= 8                         # desertions next (step 26)

# army effectiveness (+0x04)
per_point = bill.effectiveness
if army_effectiveness < 100:
    per_point = per_point / min(100 - army_effectiveness, 20)
paid.effectiveness = min(paid.effectiveness, bill.effectiveness * 3 / 2)
while paid.effectiveness >= per_point and per_point > 0:   # verified (issue #11): 150 at 15/point = +10
    army_effectiveness = clamp(army_effectiveness + 1, 0, 100)
    paid.effectiveness -= per_point

# violence (+0x08)
if paid.violence >= bill.violence - bill.violence / 10 and violence > 0:
    violence -= 1

# loan (+0x0C)
bank += paid.loan                              # money class 28ec:00b3
if bank >= 0: loan_payment (+0x1A4) = 0

# planets (+0x10): not paying plans a civil war
if paid.planets < bill.planets:
    short = (bill.planets - paid.planets) / (bill.planets / 1000 + 1)   # per mille
    k = (planets - 3 * n[G]) * short / 2000    # government planets soften it
    if k > 0:
        r = clamp(planets / k, 1, 10000)
        flags(+0x1C4) |= 1
        total = 0
        for t in 0..9: plan[t] = Planets[t].count / r;  total += plan[t]
        repeat at most 100 times while total < k:
            t = rnd(10)
            if Planets[t].count > plan[t]: plan[t] += 1;  total += 1
        # plan = int32[10] at +0x1C7, executed by the civil war step

# donation (+0x14)
if paid.donation > bill.donation:
    extra = (paid.donation - bill.donation) / (taxable + 1)
    if extra > 1000: extra -= 1000             # as in the original
    if extra > 0: favor (+0x1B0) += int16(extra)
coordinator_treasury (Galaxy +0x3AC) += paid.donation / 1000

# efficiency (+0x1B4)
if planets > 0 and taxable < 2,000,000:
    efficiency = (taxable * 1000 - sum of all six bill lines) / planets
```

Turn-5 sample: efficiency 1090 with taxable 625 and 357 planets implies a
bill of about 236,000 credits, consistent in size with the formulas.

## Military consequences (turn step 26, `44e1:0000`)

```
if int8 +0x1C6 >= 0:                            # verified (issue #2)
    army_effectiveness = clamp(army_effectiveness + int8 +0x1C5, 0, 100)
else:
    army_effectiveness = 0
    if flags(+0x1C4) & 8:
        d = clamp(-int8 +0x1C6, 0, 20)          # percent
        each of soldiers, fighters, defense stations, heavy cruisers,
        generals, carriers, light cruisers loses unit * d / 100
        # "N troops desert you", "N generals leave your army",
        # "fighters decay due to lack of maintainance funds", ...
```

Flag bits 0..3 of `+0x1C4`, `+0x1C5` and `+0x1C6` are cleared by
`1e7b:0f61` and when an empire is created (`48cb:0254`). `1e7b:0f61` is
called (conditionally, `1e7b:0532`) by the play-session function
`1e7b:0197` **before** its turn loop (`1e7b:0669` calls the turn driver),
so once per session. They are **also cleared during every turn**
(observed in issue #10: a hungry turn's −21 was not applied again in the
next turn of the same session); the clearing step is not located yet
(`RE-CHECK(field)`), so the port clears them at the start of each turn.

## Empire fields found here

- `+0x170` int8: army effectiveness, percent (100 after reset).
- `+0x190` int16: violence/unrest level 0..7 (`state`).
- `+0x19C` int32: bank balance; negative = loan.
- `+0x1A4` int32: loan payment due per year.
- `+0x1B4` int32: efficiency (income per planet after expenses).
- `+0x1C4` flags: bit 0 planned civil war, bit 3 army shortfall (unpaid
  or underfed military).
- `+0x1C5`, `+0x1C6` int8: military payment shortfall and resulting
  effectiveness.
```

`docs/game/food.md`:

```md
# Food market and feeding (turn step 12)

`512e:018b` (step 12 of `turn.md`): the food market ("Food is in ...
demand", "Current quantity available is ...", Buy / Sell / Visit Bank /
Continue), then the feeding screen ("Your people require N megatons",
"Your Army needs N", "Failure to feed your people/army will lead to civil
war and/or loss ...", "Do you wish to reconsider your actions").
Transcribed from the disassembly, **not yet checked against a sample**
(except buying and selling food, the food needs and starvation:
verified in issues #1, #2, #3 and #9, `verification.md`):
`RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in `production.md`.

## Helpers

```
# 512e:0105  food needed per turn
need_people = population * 38 / 100
need_army   = soldiers * 3 / 100

# 512e:0000  food price per megaton, for a market quantity q
food_price(q):
    q = max(galaxy.food_market (+0x388) + q, 0)
    return 85 - q / 2000 if q < 160000 else 5

# 512e:0072  demand word shown with the price: thresholds 10, 20, 40, 60,
# 80 on food_price (strings DS:3be1, 3bea, 3bee, 3bf7, 3bfe, 3c03).
```

## Market

```
surplus   = food_stock (+0x18C) - need_people - need_army
buy_price = food_price(surplus)        # your own surplus moves the price (verified)
sell_price = buy_price / 2             # verified (49 -> 24)

Buy N  (N <= min(money / buy_price, galaxy.food_market);
        the suggested amount is the shortfall, clamped to that maximum):
    money -= N * buy_price                       # money class 28ec:0199
    if coordinator_treasury < 1,500,000,000:
        coordinator_treasury += N * buy_price / 1000
    food_stock += N;  galaxy.food_market -= N

Sell N (N <= food_stock):
    money += N * sell_price
    coordinator_treasury = max(coordinator_treasury - N * sell_price / 1000, 0)  # RE-CHECK: not observed (sales < 1000 credits)
    food_stock -= N;  galaxy.food_market += N
```

The prices are computed once when the screen opens, not after each
trade. The menu loops until Continue ('C'); "Visit Bank" calls the Solar
Bank (`3e40:0000`).

## Feeding

The feeding screen works on a copy of the Empire block `+0x1BA` ..
`+0x226` (turn state: `+0x1BA`, taxable income `+0x1BC`, flags `+0x1C4`,
`+0x1C5`, `+0x1C6`, civil war plan `+0x1C7`, ...), lets the player give
food to the people and then to the army (each capped by the stock and by
the need), and on confirmation writes the copy back together with the
remaining food stock (`512e:0e75`). A shortfall is turned into events in
that copy (civil war / losses, applied by later turn steps).

## Starvation (`512e:0c2a` .. `0e16`)

The player types how much to give each side (people first, capped by
the need and the stock). A shortfall only sets fields in the turn
state; the damage is done by later turn steps:

```
if fed_people < need_people:
    flags(+0x1C4) |= 2                                   # insurgents
    int32 +0x223 = max(0, population * (need_people - fed_people)
                          / need_people)                 # insurgent strength
if fed_army < need_army:
    s = -(39 * (need_army - fed_army) / need_army)       # 0 .. -39
    int8 +0x1C5 = min(int8 +0x1C5, s)                    # effectiveness change
    flags(+0x1C4) |= 8
```

- **People** (turn step 25, `civil-war.md`, insurgents branch): the
  riots kill and take planets and military in proportion to
  `+0x223 * 100 / population`, capped at **30 %**; violence + 1. The
  population there is the one **after** this turn's growth (step 22), so
  the riot is smaller than the share left unfed: feeding 90 % of 159 M
  people (`+0x223` = 15) with +157 M growth gave 15 × 100 / 316 = 4 %.
  Feeding nobody or half usually gives the full 30 %. Protection does not
  prevent the riot. Verified exactly (issue #1, `verification.md`).
- **Army** (turn step 26, `expenses.md`): army effectiveness drops by up
  to 39 points. Desertions also need the military **payment** shortfall
  (`+0x1C6 < 0`), so an army that is paid but hungry loses effectiveness
  only. Verified exactly (issue #2): half fed (1 of 2), 100 → 81, no
  desertions.
- Before confirming, "Failure to feed your people/army will lead to
  civil war and/or loss of forces." / "Do you wish to reconsider your
  actions" loops back to the screen.

`+0x223` is overwritten, not added to, so it keeps only this turn's
shortfall.
```

`docs/game/maintenance.md`:

```md
# Maintenance (hourly and daily)

`5680:0c52`, run inside the game lock (`5221:04a8` / `04c2`). Partly
transcribed from the disassembly, **not checked against the game**:
`RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in `production.md`; `now`
is the current time (`DS:bbb9`), Galaxy fields are in
`docs/formats/galaxy.md`.

Nothing runs once `now` is past Galaxy `+0x50` (an end date; after a
reset it is `0x7FFEC750`, Jan 2038, i.e. "never").

## Planet regeneration (`1c59:0855`, first thing in the maintenance)

```
if now > galaxy.last_regen (+0x48) and galaxy.regen_seconds (+0x38C) > 0:
    if galaxy.planets_market (+0x392) < 30000:
        n = (now - last_regen) / (regen_seconds + 1)
        if n > 0:
            planets_market += n
            last_regen += n * (regen_seconds + 1)
    else:
        last_regen = now
```

Verified in size on the samples: the market went from 44 to 28,544
between two sessions (3-second setting, about 32 hours of game clock).

## Local-play defaults (`5221:0112`)

Sets the Galaxy to: maintenance every day, food market 7,000,000,
regeneration 3 seconds, 100 planets in the market, no per-turn planet
limit (...). Probably applied for "This game is configured for LOCAL PLAY
ONLY" (`RE-CHECK(logic)`: when it is called).

## Hourly ("Running hourly maintenance...")

```
while now - galaxy.last_hourly (+0x3BA) > 3600:
    for p in 1..9: pirate_hourly(p)       # 4b5f:034a, below
    galaxy.last_hourly += 3600
```

### Pirate growth (`4b5f:034a`)

For each pirate team `n` (its number `+0x20`, 1..9), once per elapsed
hour (its own time stamp is `+0x22`). `pl[t]` = the pirate's planets of
type `t` (`+0xB4 + 2*t`, `PETFROGUSA`). Each line applies only while the
stock is below its cap. Caps and constants are transcribed; the exact
form of the growth terms is `RE-CHECK(formula)` (the `/ 10` and shift
operands were read from compact listings).

| Stock | Cap | Growth per hour |
|---|---|---|
| soldiers `+0x98` | n × 3000 | `rnd(100)` + supply planets × 5 / 10 |
| fighters `+0x9C` | n × 3000 | `rnd(100)` + supply planets (shifted) / 10 |
| heavy cruisers `+0xA4` | n × 3000 | `rnd(100)` + supply planets / 10 |
| defense stations `+0xA0` | n × 3000 | `rnd(100)` + supply planets (shifted) / 10 |
| carriers `+0xA8` | n × 300 | `rnd(10)` + supply planets / 10 |
| generals `+0xAC` | n × 300 | `rnd(10)` + supply planets / 10 |
| covert agents `+0xB0` | n × 500 | `rnd(10)` |
| food `+0x94` | n × 10,000,000 | `rnd(30)` + food planets × 6 |
| credits `+0x90` | n × 10,000,000 | n × 10000 + pl[P] × 230 + pl[E] × 50 + pl[T] × 260 + pl[O] × 210 + pl[U] × 70 |
| covert agents `+0xB0` (again) | n × 10000 | + pl[G] |

So higher-numbered teams grow bigger, and the planets they take in
revolts (`events.md`) make them richer.

## Daily ("Running daily maintenance...")

Runs when `now - galaxy.last_daily (+0x40) >= days (+0x39C) * 86400`, in
this order:

1. **Backups**: every `Data/X.II` is copied to `Backup/X.II`.
2. **News**: `News/NEWS9.MSG` is deleted and `NEWS0..8` shift up one day.
3. **"Searching for illegal nuclear bomb traders..."** (`5b69:0228`), then
   the daily news (`5680:0160`, newspaper state Galaxy `+0x3C0`) and
   investments (`4c47:32f1`).
4. **Nuclear weapons supply**, presumably:
   ```
   g.x3B2 += 2 if g.x3B2 > 400 else 5 if g.x3B2 > 300 else 15
   if g.x3B4 < 30: g.x3B4 += 1
   ```
5. **Psionic bomb price** (Galaxy `+0x3C2`, `events.md`): `price = max(price * 15 / 20, 5,000,000)`.
6. **"Checking top scores and lottery..."**:
   - First, for every empire: if its last-played time (`+0x28`) is older
     than Galaxy `+0x44` it is set to Galaxy `+0x44`; then the per-empire
     daily update below runs.
   - The lottery draw (`5680:1213`):
     ```
     w = rand() * tickets / 32768        # tickets = Galaxy +0x3A4
     if tickets <= 0: w = -1, tickets = 0
     for each empire e (in slot order):
         if w >= 0 and e.tickets (+0x172) > w:
             winner = e; galaxy.last_winner (+0x3A6) = e
             prize = tickets * 11000 + 3,000,000           # 55e6:0000
             galaxy.last_prize (+0x3A8) = prize
             bank += prize if bank < 2,000,000,000 else money += prize
         w -= e.tickets;  e.tickets = 0
     ```
   - The day's Masters, one pass over all empires:
     ```
     best = {solar: 10000, planet: 300, weapons: 50000}   # minimums
     for each empire e, for (title, value) in
             (solar, score), (planet, planets), (weapons, net worth):
         if value(e) > best[title] * 3 / 2:
             master[title] = e;  best[title] = value(e)
         elif value(e) >= best[title]:
             master[title] = none;  best[title] = value(e)
     ```
     A Master needs a 50 % lead over everyone else (and over the minimum).
     Masters are Galaxy `+0x396` (Solar), `+0x398` (Planet), `+0x39A`
     (Weapons), -1 = none.
   - Rewards: each Master gets tournament points in Empire int32 `+0x178`
     from the resources `Points.SolarMaster` (default 5),
     `Points.PlanetMaster` (1), `Points.WeaponsMaster` (1). The Solar
     Master also gets `money += coordinator_treasury * 10` while the
     treasury only loses 1 % (`treasury -= treasury / 100`); as in the
     original. ("... has been chosen today's Solar Master, and has
     received a N credit bonus!")
7. **Defense pacts of a new Weapons Master** (`5680:19b4`..`1d71`): when
   the Weapons Master changes ("X has been chosen the new Weapons Master")
   and the new one has more than 500 planets, each of its treaties that
   carries an ally contribution (soldiers % or cruisers % > 0, i.e. the
   defense pacts) is turned into a Neutrality/Peace Treaty (kind 1) on
   both sides, keeping byte 0 (", and lost some defense pacts").
8. **Interest rate** (Galaxy `+0x3BE`), only when the game is registered
   (`System +0x128`; the port is always "registered"):
   ```
   if rate < 3:      rate += 2   # "go up to N% as the galaxy's economy booms!"
   elif rate > 10:   rate -= 3   # "fall sharply to N% as pirate raids increase!"
   elif rnd(8) == 0: rate -= 2   # "fall to N% in response to a weakening economy."
   elif rnd(5) == 0: rate -= 1   # "fall slightly to N%."
   elif rnd(3) == 0: rate += 1   # "rise to N%."
   ```
9. `galaxy.last_daily = now`, `galaxy.last_hourly = now`.

Bank interest is not part of the maintenance: it is applied every turn
(`bank.md`). 

## Per-empire daily update (`5680:1f8f`)

Run for each existing empire during the daily maintenance:

```
e.turns_per_day (+0x198) = galaxy.turns_per_interval (+0x39E)
e.turns_used (+0x196) = 0
e.inactive_days_left (+0x2A1) -= 1
e.attacks (+0x229) = 0
for objects at +0x23B, +0x23F, +0x247: 14f6:0267      # also turn step 13
for each treaty t: if t.byte0 > 0: t.byte0 -= 1     # days left on the treaty
if resource DeleteDeadPlayers (default yes):
    if e has a name and (planets == 0 or population == 0):
        "Player X has collapsed!" / "has abdicated!"; erase
    elif e.inactive_days_left <= 0:
        "Empire X erased - inactive for N days."     # N = InactiveTimeOut
        erase
erase = 6923:057d (remove from the galaxy) + 48cb:0254 (re-initialize slot)
```

`inactive_days_left` is refilled from the resource `InactiveTimeOut`
(default 10) every time the player plays (`1e7b:0569`), and starts at 4
for a new slot.
```

```md
# Messages (turn step 19)

Segment `58b5`, stored in `Message.II` (stream format, `II.md`). UI-heavy;
the port can reimplement it freely while keeping these features:

- **Writing** (`58b5:0b54`, `58b5:195c`): a line editor with a ruler;
  commands `/S` (save), `=abort`, `=list`, `=clear`; a limited number of
  lines ("You have N lines for the message").
- **Addressing** (`58b5:181e`): "Choose Empires [* for a public message]",
  or All. A public message stays up 1..30 days ("How many days would you
  like to leave this public message up?").
- **Flags** (`58b5:054b`): anonymous, public, non-player, sysop; the
  header shows From / To / Flags, and for the sysop the real sender and
  the date (`58b5:0868`).
- **Reading** (`58b5:1eb3`): Reply, Quoted Reply, Delete or Keep (keys
  `KRDQ`); replies can be posted publicly, copied to all original
  recipients, and can include the original anonymous author. Messages can
  also be "reported by a spy" (intercepted through covert Infiltration,
  `attacks.md`).
- Turn step 19 also decrements Empire byte `+0x2D3` when it is above 0
  (`58b5:1ce9`); `RE-CHECK(field)`: probably the messages left to send
  this turn or the days of a public post.
```

`docs/game/population.md`:

```md
# Population (turn step 22)

`5f37:0000` (step 22 of `turn.md`). Population is in millions (Empire
`+0x184`). Transcribed from the disassembly, **not yet checked against a
sample**: every formula is `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port. Notation as in
`production.md` (`rnd(k)` = `rand() * k / 32768`, divisions truncate toward
zero); `planets` = total planets, `state` = violence level (`+0x190`),
`tax` = tax rate (`+0x1AA`), `pollution` = `+0x188`.

The `rand()` calls happen in this order: births, deaths, then the
"people love thee" roll.

```
# births
births = (pop + n[U]*101 + planets/2) / (rnd(10) + 23) + 1

# deaths (crowding)
deaths = pop * (pop / (rnd(10) + 17)) / (planets + 1) / 10

# emigration
emig  = pop * (state*state + 1) / 80
emig += emig * (tax*tax + 1) / 200
emig += planets * n[T] / 100000
emig += pollution / 100

# immigration
immig = (pop + 36 * n[E] * prod[E]) / (state*state + 50)
immig = immig * (100 - tax) * (100 - tax) / 10000

# more deaths
deaths += n[O] / 10                              # mining
poll_deaths = max(pollution * 10 / (planets + 1), 0)
deaths += poll_deaths

emig = max(emig, 0)
if pop > 2,000,000,000: immig = 0; births = 0

# never lose more people than there are
k = 0
while emig + deaths > pop and k < 100:
    emig -= emig / 7;  deaths -= deaths / 7;  k += 1
while emig + deaths > pop: emig -= 1
deaths = min(deaths, pop)

births, deaths, immig, emig = max(each, 0)
poll_deaths = min(poll_deaths, deaths)

pop = max(pop + births + immig - emig - deaths, 0)
```

Report (each line only when its value is positive): "N million people
were born in your empire", "N million citizens die[, including N million
from galactic pollution]", "N million people immigrate to your empire",
"N million citizens emigrate from your empire", "A net population change
of N million people".

"Your people love thee and hope you rule forever!" is printed when
`rnd(10) == 0`, bits 0..3 of Empire byte `+0x1C4` are clear, pollution is
0, Empire int32 `+0x1B0` > 0 and the violence level is 0. It has no other
effect.

After the report, `43df:0f44` is called (desertions, see `turn.md`).

```

`docs/game/production.md`:

```md
# Production (turn step 8)

`4629:0b58` (step 8 of `turn.md`) calls `4629:0000`, which computes the
turn's production into a 0x4C-byte result, applies it to the empire, and
returns; `4629:0b58` then reports it and adds the light cruisers.
Transcribed from the disassembly. **Not yet checked against a sample**
(the two samples are 5 turns apart, with purchases in between), so every
formula is `RE-CHECK(formula)` in the port until a per-turn snapshot
confirms it.

Notation: `n[X]` = planet count of type X, `prod[X]` = the type's current
production per planet (`Planets[X] +0x8`, see `docs/formats/empire.md`).
All values are int32, divisions truncate toward zero (Borland `LDIV@`).
`rand()` is Borland's (0..32767); `rnd(k)` below means `rand() * k / 32768`
(0..k-1). "money +=" goes through the money class `28ec:00b3`.
`taxable` accumulates a value stored into Empire `+0x1BC` at the end.

## Order of evaluation

```
taxable = 0

# Food (result +0x10)
if n[F] != 0:
    food = max(n[F] * prod[F] - pollution / 10, 0)
    food_stock (+0x18C) += food

# Ore (result +0x0C)
if n[O] != 0:
    ore = n[O] * prod[O]
    if n[O] < 100:
        repeat n[O] times: ore += rnd(100)        # one rand() per planet
    ore = max(ore, 0)
    money += ore;  taxable += ore / 1000

# Supply (results +0x1C .. +0x36)
if n[S] != 0:
    p = n[S] * prod[S]
    soldiers   = p * pct_soldiers  (+0x297) / 100
    fighters   = p * pct_fighters  (+0x298) / 130
    stations   = p * pct_stations  (+0x299) / 170
    generals   = p * pct_generals  (+0x29C) / 700
    carriers   = p * pct_carriers  (+0x29B) / 950
    cruisers   = p * pct_cruisers  (+0x29A) / 1200
    spent      = (soldiers*10 + fighters*13 + stations*17 + generals*70
                  + carriers*95 + cruisers*120) / 10
    credits    = (p - spent) * 100
    add each unit to its Empire field; money += credits
    taxable += credits / 1000

# Tourism (result +0x08); two rand() calls, in this order
if n[T] != 0:
    a = rnd(1000); b = rnd(1000)
    tour = n[T] * (prod[T] + a - b - state * 350 - pollution / 10)
    tour = max(tour, 0);  money += tour;  taxable += tour / 1000

# Urban (result +0x04)
if n[U] != 0:
    urban = max(n[U] * (prod[U] - state * state), 0)    # int16 product
    money += urban;  taxable += urban / 1000

# Petroleum (result +0x00, +0x14)
if n[P] != 0:
    oil = max(n[P] * oil_price(), 0)              # oil_price = 48cb:1196
    money += oil;  taxable += oil / 1000
    if oil_price() > 10000: taxable += oil / 3000  # called a second time
    pollution (+0x188) += max(n[P], 0)

# Anti-pollution (result +0x18)
if n[A] != 0:
    clean = clamp(n[A] * prod[A], 0, pollution)
    pollution = max(pollution - clean, 0)

# Research
if n[R] != 0:
    r = max(n[R] * prod[R], 0)
    research (+0x293) = min(research + r, 100000)

# Taxes (result +0x38)
if population > 0:
    tax = population * tax_rate (+0x1AA, int8) * 3 / (state + 1)
    for i in 0..24:                               # trade treaties
        if relation[i].kind == 2 and empire[i] has a name:
            tax += rnd(16) * empire[i].population # rand() << 4 >> 15
    tax = max(tax, 0);  money += tax;  taxable += tax / 1000

Empire +0x1BC = taxable                           # 28ec:0094

# Back in 4629:0b58, after the report of food:
if n[R] > 0:
    lc = n[R] * 10 / (light_cruisers / 70 + 10)
    if lc > 0: light_cruisers (+0x2F0) += lc
```

`state` is Empire `+0x190` (int16, 0..7). `relation[i]` is the 4-byte
entry at Empire `+0x0EC + 4*i`, `kind` its low 5 bits of byte 1.

The `rand()` call order matters for reproducing a turn exactly: ore
(per planet, only below 100 ore planets), then tourism (two), then trade
treaties (one per treaty partner).

## Report strings (4629:0b58)

"megatons of food grown" / "... were grown, due to excessive pollution",
"light cruisers were produced by your research planets", "Your supply
planets produce ...", "credits worth of ore has been mined", "credits have
been earned from tourist attractions" (+ "possibly due to the poor
conditions in your empire"), "credits were collected as trade taxes on
urban planets", "credits have been earned from petroleum pumping",
"exatons of pollutants have been ... the galactic atmosphere", "You
collect ... credits in taxes".

## Production drift (turn step 27, `14f6:02a6`), verified

After the turn, each planet type's current production per planet
(`Planets[t] +0x8`) moves toward its base value (`+0x4`):

```
for t in 0..9:
    d = base - current if base >= 0 else 0
    if d >= 30 or d <= -30: current += d / 30      # truncates toward zero
    elif base > current:    current += 1
    elif base < current:    current -= 1
```

On the `turn5` → `turn6` sample this gives exactly the observed values
(Ore 2455 → 2447, Tourism 3031 → 3019, Education 34 → 33, Food 48 → 47,
Urban 205 → 204). Current production starts above base after a reset and
is raised by research (`events.md`), then decays back.

```

```md
# One turn (SRE 0.994b)

The turn driver is `1e7b:0731` (resident code, so its decompilation is
reliable; the steps it calls live in overlays and are reached through
stubs, resolved by `tools/disasm.py`). It runs these steps in order for the
current empire; field names refer to `docs/formats/empire.md`.

Most steps are followed by a call to `48cb:2454`, which adjusts the turn
counters (`+0x194`, `+0x196`) and `+0x1BA` (reset to 21); probably the
rollback when the player aborts the turn (`RE-CHECK(logic)`).

| 20 | `0d92` | attack menu (`attacks.md`) | `508f:0121` | "Attack Options", "Conventional Invasion", "Guerilla Ambush", "Pirate Raid", "Nuclear Offensive", "Chemical Warfare" |
| 21 | `0ddf` | end of turn: last-turn notice, income | `5f37:07ae` | "This is your last turn today."; reads money, `+0x1BC` |
| 22 | `0dfc` | **population** (`population.md`) | `5f37:0000` | "A net population change of"; uses population, state, urban planets |
| 23 | `0e0d` | **score**: `score -= score / 19; score += planets / 6 + population / (tax + 10)` (verified, `verification.md`) | `48cb:26b0` | |
| 24 | `0e1a` | Coordinator favor update (`civil-war.md`) | `48cb:2731` | `+0x1B0` |
| 25 | `0e30` | **civil war / riots**, Coordinator aid (`civil-war.md`) | `44e1:07cc` | "CIVIL WAR", "riots"; lost planets return to the Galaxy market |
| 26 | `0e44` | army effectiveness, desertions from unpaid military (`expenses.md`) | `44e1:0000` | "troops desert you" |
| 27 | `0e55` | **production drift**: each planet type's current production moves toward its base (verified, `production.md`) | `48cb:267c` → `14f6:02a6` | |
| 28 | `0eb6`, `0ec3` | release the game state and announce the day's Masters (nothing reaches the disk here, see below) | `5221:04f9`, `5221:052e` | "Today's Solar Master is", "Planet Master", Galaxy `+0x396..0x39A` |

Steps between `09c5` and `0d22` print the end-of-turn summary table
(`43df:0b60` asks y/n questions there).

**Interrupted turns** (observed in issue #11): a turn broken off in the
middle (Ctrl+C in DOSBox, after the status screen) was saved with its
production already applied, and the next session printed "Continuing
previously interrupted turn..." (`1e7b:0197`, test `+0x1BA > 1`) and went
on from the expenses, without producing again. Empire int16 `+0x1BA`
appears to hold the turn step reached (`RE-CHECK(field)`).

**When the files are written** (observed in DOSBox, 2026-10-21): during a
session the game keeps the galaxy in memory. Across a whole turn, and the
start of the next one, `EMPIRE.II`, `GALAXY.II`, `PIRATE.II` and
`SYSTEM.II` stayed byte for byte the same on disk; only `PLAYER.II` and the
message, trading, event and news files were rewritten. The four were
written together when the player left the game. `TRADING.II` is the
exception seen so far: a deal is written to it as soon as it is sent
(issue #7), so the partner can receive it while the sender still plays. A snapshot of a given
turn therefore needs the player to quit right after it.

## Next

The bold steps are transcribed in their own files but not yet checked
against a sample: that needs per-turn snapshots (save before and after
one turn, quitting the game right after it) to replay a turn and compare. The maintenance (between sessions) is in `maintenance.md`. Remaining:
the rest of the bank and buy/sell, attacks, covert operations, random
events and the hourly pirate update.
```

`docs/original-bugs.md`:

```md
# Bugs in the original SRE 0.994b

Behaviour of the original that the port must **not** reproduce (or must
reproduce only where file compatibility needs it). Each entry says how it was
found and what is still unknown.

## Y2K: game "not reset" with a current date (cause found)

- **Seen:** in DOSBox with the host date (2026), `SRE RESET` completes,
  but `SRE` then says the game has not been reset. With the date faked to
  1999 (`faketime`), reset and play work.
- **Cause:** the System record check `6c37:02c9`, called by `main`
  (`1848:04d3`), accepts `SYSTEM.II` only when both of its time stamps
  (`+0x120`, `+0x124`, written at reset by `6c37:011d`) lie strictly
  between `0x12C684C0` (315,000,000 s = 1979-12-25) and `0x38538E40`
  (945,000,000 s = **1999-12-12**), and the registered flag `+0x128` is
  0..5. A reset made after 12 December 1999 stores a time stamp above the
  window, so the check fails and `main` prints "Sorry, this game has not
  been reset." Any date before 12 Dec 1999 works (the samples are stamped
  13 Jan 1999).
- **Workaround for the original:** only the reset needs the fake date.
  The check reads the two time stamps written into `SYSTEM.II` by
  `SRE RESET`, which never change afterwards, so once the galaxy is reset
  under a pre-1999-12-12 date (e.g. `faketime '1999-01-13' dosbox ...`),
  `SRE` can be played with the real date. Confirmed in practice: the
  galaxy here was reset with a fake date and the turns were then played.
- **Port (required fix):** the remake must not have this window. Use
  64-bit `std::chrono` / `time_t` everywhere, never reject a galaxy because
  of its creation date, and when importing original `.II` files accept any
  time stamp. See `DESIGN.md`.

## `checksum16` loses its high word

`(r << 16) | s` is evaluated in 16 bits, so the checksum is only the
Fletcher-style sum `s` (see `formats/II.md`). Harmless; needed only to read
or write original `.II` files.

## Conventional attack: wrong pool in one loss list (suspected)

- **Code:** in the battle loop of `3b7a:0325`, the fifth duel (defender's
  command ship hits) passes the defender's light-cruiser pool (`bp-0x38`)
  in the attacker's loss list (`3b7a:1289`).
- **Effect (from reading):** once the attacker has no heavy cruisers,
  those hits destroy the defender's own light cruisers.
- **Port:** decide when testing; see `docs/game/attacks.md`.

## Capped loans add no yearly payment (suspected)

- **Code:** when a loan would push money past 2,000,000,000, the bank
  (`3e40:1002`) pays it out in chunks and then jumps to the end of the
  loan code (`3e40:1116`), skipping `Empire[+0x1A4] += yearly_payment`.
- **Effect (from reading):** that loan is never billed through the
  yearly payment; only the per-turn interest grows the debt.
- **Port:** always add the yearly payment for what was actually lent.

```

```TXT
PROBLEMS (Q) AND ANSWERS (A) FOR SRE!          [last updated 12/30/92]
哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I can't figure out why ...
A.  Check SYSOP.LOG.  It records any errors that SRE detects.  If you
    report bugs to us, it may help if you include the contents of that
    file.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I can't get any flavors to work.
A.  Be sure you are putting FLAVOR, not FLAVORS, as the resource.dat
    option.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I am registered but I can't get nuclear & chemical weapons to show
    up on the menu.
A.  Each player will need to find nuclear, chemical, and psionic weapons.
    Since they are outlawed by the Galactic Coordinator, they are not easily
    available; I suggest keeping more covert agents than planets so that the
    agents will search the planets looking for people who can sell you a
    nuclear / chemical weapon.  If one is found, a question will be asked ("Do
    you wish to buy a nuclear weapon?") in the profits/ news screen.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I don't run a BBS, but I would like to play SRE.
A.  1.  Run INSTALL
    2.  During the installation process, select LOCAL play.  It will
        create a batch file that will ask for your name and then run
        SRE.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  SRDOOR doesn't read the door file correctly.
A.  We have tested SRDOOR for DOOR.SYS and DORINFO1.DEF.  If you are
    unable to use these, you may be able to experiment with the formats
    for other BBSes.  Unfortunately, we have not fully tested the other
    BBS formats.  If you have any information about the door file
    produced by your BBS, please send us a letter!

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I get an error message about running SRDOOR!
A.  Run INSTALL SRE to install the correct BBS type for your system.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  SRE doesn't read the ANSI status of the user.
A.  SRE currently ignores the ANSI status, even though it's in the door
    file, so that users can play black and white if they'd like.  (It's
    faster without color!)

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I can't figure out what to put in my batch file to run SRE.
A.  Run INSTALL to set up a batch file automatically.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I don't know how to set up my BBS software to run SRE.
A.  Consult your BBS manual for more information.  Look for information
    on running DOORS.  You also need to produce a DOOR FILE when running
    SRE.  Select a door file format that is compatible with the options
    listed in INSTALL.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I have a high speed modem running at locked baud rates.
A.  Read Resource.Doc for the "LockBaudRate" parameter, which lets you
    tell SRE that you're using locked baud rates.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I get snow on my CGA monitor.
A.  Use the Display.Video resource to set up BIOS calls.  See
    Resource.HLP for details.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  SRE runs too slowly.
A.  Get a faster computer!  :)

    If you have EMS or XMS memory, you should set SRE's swapping so
    that it doesn't swap to disk.  Look at Resource.DOC for more
    details.  Also, try changing the display parameter in the
    resource file.  Turning off special effects might also help.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪

A.  Be sure to use
        Display.Video                   BIOS
    and
        Display.VGA                     off

    when running under DESQview.  (See Resource.HLP if you want
    details.)

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I have a monochrome monitor.  How can I play locally without color?
A.  Use the /ANSI=0 switch to turn off ANSI color.  Also use BIOS
    video option to make sure SRE is compatible with your monochrome
    display card.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  My modem buffer causes the pauses and Yes/No prompts to be
    extremely slow on the remote side.
A.  Use the /NOSPECIALEFFECTS switch to turn off the special effects
    at the pauses and Yes/No prompts.  Alternatively, (preferably)
    you can edit RESOURCE.DAT to set up your system configuration.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I want to know what the users have done in SRE.
A.  Use the LOG option in Resource.dat to write all output to a file
    Note: this file is overwritten every time SRE runs, so you should
    save it somewhere if you want the log of more than one user.  You
    can do this in your batch file with:
        SRE             (already in the file)
        TYPE SRE.LOG >>ALLUSERS.LOG

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I want a separate file to contain the scores.
A.  SRE automatically creates SRESCORE.ANS (ANSI file) and
    SRESCORE.MSG (non-ANSI file) when it runs.  You can modify
    RESOURCE.DAT to write the score files anywhere you want.

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪
Q.  I want to register but I don't want my name to appear.
A.  Your name will appear at the end of the game in the registered
    version.  We do not register to your handle for legal reasons.
    (A handle is not a legal recipient of registration benefits.)
    Sorry!

哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪哪

A.  Don't worry!  All registerers of SRE will NOT be added to any

Q.  Why is there no full editor in SRE?
```

```DOC
  LACK OF REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS
ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ

Registration is NOT required to run SRE.  SRE might be classified as one of
these types of programs:

Shareware - Yes!  SRE is shareware.  You are required to register this game
            after 99 years of trial use!
Freeware - Yes!  SRE could be considered freeware.  (However, freeware is
            a trademarked term.)  You are not required to pay any fee for
            this program.  However, we do give benefits to those who donate
            $15 or more.
Crippleware - Yes!  SRE is slightly crippled!  You can't access the bank in
            the unregistered version.  (But you don't need the bank to play
            the game.)
Bogusware - Yes!  SRE is bogusware!  It will destroy itself after 99 years!
            (If you don't register!)  (just kidding!)
Deadware - Yes!  You must've found the bugs!
Bonusware - Yes!  If you register, you get bonuses (like the bank)!

(I prefer to think of it as Bonusware.)

ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ
  REGISTRATION COST
ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ

Seriously,

Registrationј is only $15 (U.S. dollars) for SRE 0.99x, so go ahead and
register!  All we want to know is some basic information, and if you like,
you can fill out the survey as well.  We may use survey results to determine
what operating systems, machines, and BBS software to support in future games.

*** To register, fill out Docs/SREReg.TXT and send it in.јј ***

What we do is send you a registration code that you type into SRE and it
will register itself.  We do not create a 'registered version' or send you
a disk.  The reason?  In many games, you can register one version and the
next version requires a new fee for upgrade.  For SRE, you get the numbers
that work in ALL versions of SRE.  That way, you will be able to get all
future versions for free from local BBSes.

NOTE: We do not register this game under handles (for various reasons).
      If you wish to see where your name will appear, run SRE SYSOP
      and choose "Registered Version".

Non-US persons:  Checks / money orders must be US funds from a U.S. bank.
                 Otherwise, send US cash or an international money order.
                 (in Canada, the Post Office can issue Money Orders in
                 U.S. funds.)

                 You may also wish to get together with other sysops in
                 your area to register together; you will save on the
                 currency conversion charges and also on postage.  I
                 will send the registrations to each person separately.

Make out checks or money orders to "Amit J. Patel".  Sorry, NO credit card
orders.  Expect 2-3 weeks to receive your numbers.  We try to handle
everything as fast as possible, but sometimes it just doesn't get done
soon enough.

Registration is not required in order to run this game, but we'd like
you to register this game!  The benefits of registering are:

  ў Automatic registration of all new versions.  (See above.)
  ў The Bank - loan, savings, and investments
  ў More Attack types - chemical, nuclear, and psionic
  ў Customization - you can set the number of turns, the number of
    planets available, the galactic tax rate, and the bank interest.

Please first evaluate this software and determine whether users on your BBS
enjoy it; it makes little sense to register a program without trying it out,
then later complaining that nobody likes it!

If you have any more questions, please send a letter to the address listed in
the registration form.

Thanks for registering!

--
ј By "Registration", I'm NOT trying to imply that you MUST register, like
  many other programs; this program IS free, but the "registration fee" is a
  donation to enable extra features in the game.  You are NOT required
  to register, like most shareware programs.

јј Registration takes several weeks (2 to 4); if you wish to avoid delays,
   please do the following:
        1 - Type the information into SREREG.TXT and then print it out
            instead of writing it by hand.
        2 - If you are registering more than one game, please print out
            separate registration forms and include separate checks.  Mehul
            and I are _not_ the same person!  If you send a form to him,
            and you write at the bottom "register SRE also", I will not
            read that form until 3 weeks after he gets it (he has to finish
            the registration first), and then it may be ANOTHER 3 weeks
            before I do registrations.
        3 - If you must write the information by hand, please write neatly!
            Many times, we have gotten mail back from the post office because
            we were unable to read the address and our interpretation wasn't
            the right one.
        4 - Use full-sized paper instead of small pieces; small slips of
            paper are more easily lost.
        5 - It does not help to send it through express mail; since it takes
            2 to 4 weeks, one or two days is not going to make a big
            difference.  Also, my experience with the postal service
            is that it usually takes 2 or 3 days for "snail" mail to
            arrive.

ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ
  SOURCE CODE TO SRE / DOOR PROGRAMMING KIT
ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ

      It is our policy not to distribute any source code for our games.
      However, we do have complete source for the DOOR portion of the
      DOOR GAME.  (We just don't release the GAME portion.)  For SRE,
      we use SRCOMM version 2.  SRCOMM 2 has modem I/O, disk I/O, a
      Resource.Dat reader, an ANSI to screen interface (so that sysops
      don't need ANSI.SYS loaded), interfaces to SRDOOR, command line
      parameter handling, error logging, transcripts of user actions, a
      cooperative multitasker, and some other little things.  My next game
      uses SRCOMM version 3.  SRCOMM 3 has the features of SRCOMM 2, but it
      is much easier to get a game started, and includes a working demo
      game.  It also has Fossil driver support, better status bar
      customization, hot key support, SRE's menu routines, time slicing
      routines, a string class, an array class, and a better Resource.Dat
      reader that can read multiple values for each resource.

      My goal is to make door game writing very simple.  Output is very
      similar to C++'s streams, with additional support for colors, but
      without support for the advanced formatting and floating point
      number output.  Here's a bit of code from the demo game included
      in SRCOMM 3:

        kout << Tab(40) << "Hi there!!\n";
        kout << "Your sysop is " << GAME.sysop << "!\n";

      For most output, you can just search and replace cout with kout,
      and add some initialization code to start the SRCOMM library, and
      things will work.

      For Turbo Pascal, we have SRCOMMP, our communication routines from
      BRE.  Unlike the C++ routines, we don't include a lot of general
      purpose utility code (like file, array, and string classes) or a
      demo game.  However, the goal is the same -- SIMPLE game writing.
      You don't have to learn a new set of output routines; you can still
      use Write and Writeln along with all the formatting that comes with
      those commands.

      Instead of Writeln('Hi there!!'), you would use
                 Writeln(Com,'Hi there!!');
      We have written a virtual device driver called Com that can works
      for both screen and remote output, and uses direct or Fossil
      communication routines.

      Both the C++ and Turbo Pascal versions of our door kits come with
      full source, but unfortunately, neither comes with good
      documentation.  :-(  The C++ version is tested with Turbo C++ 3.0
      and Borland C++ 3.0, 3.1, and 4.0.  The C++ version will work with
      Borland C++ for OS/2 in the near future.

ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ
  I CAN'T AFFORD TO REGISTER!
ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ

      If you do not have the money to register, you do not have to remove
      the game, like so many others.  You have 99 years as a "trial"
      period.  The only thing you will be missing is the ability to set the
      number of turns and set up the bank (and some other minor things).

ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ
  LIST OF GAMES
ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ

      AC6 - Alpha Colony 6
            0.950 - latest release

            AC6 is similar to SRE in style & play.  It's written by a
            different programmer in a different language; it's not exactly
            the same; it takes many of the same types of actions and extends
            them (12 types of attack instead of 5, using multiple covert
            agents in a covert op, and stocks are just some examples).
            It is not well-supported, and it still has many bugs.

      PC  - Planetary Conquest
            2.0 - latest release
            PC is no longer supported.  Registrations are not accepted;
            all registered-only features are now available in the
            unregistered version.

            Planetary Conquest is a strategy game placed on a 20x20 on-screen
            board.  There are several playing pieces, each with a different
            purpose, strength, move, and weapon.  There are Soldiers, Tanks,
            Bases, Artillery, Walls, Obstacles/Symbols, and Water.  There are
            20 scenarios that can be played by 2 to 4 players.

      SCE - Solar Conquests Elite
            1.1 - latest release
            SCE is no longer supported.  Registrations are not accepted.

            Solar Conquests Elite is similar to PC, but is based in space.
            There are 5 types of ships and several weapon/engine types.
            The game allows from 2 to 5 players to play.

      LEA - Lost Empires of Arcadia
            0.990 - latest release
            LEA is not currently supported.  Registrations are not accepted.

            Lost Empires of Arcadia is a huge game with lots of races of
            beings, castles, thieves, wizards, assassins, many types of
            warfare, etc.  There are of course, many bugs!  :(  We do not
            have the full source due to hard disk errors, so it is very
            unlikely that we will be fixing the game.  :(

      SRH - Solar Realms Hangman
            0.990 - latest release

            This is a computer version of the popular 'Hangman' game.  You
            can enter words and other players have to guess them.  The winner
            gets to enter another word or phrase, and the process continues.

      BRE - Barren Realms Elite
            0.970 - latest releases change every day, so I don't have the
            right version number.

            This is a new game that is better than SRE, not only in play,
            but in allowing you to play against other BBSes through
            Fidonet.  There are more covert ops, more trading options, a
            trading market, better warfare, nicer news files, and best of
            all - Inter-BBS operations!  (Many people feel, that for
            single-BBS play, SRE is better than BRE, but BRE shines in
            its multiple-BBS capability.)

      SRE - Solar Realms Elite
            0.994   latest release version

            SRE is this game!  SRE is different from BRE in several (small)
            ways:  (1) fewer bugs; (2) Flavors; (3) an optional
            non-inflationary economic rule set; (4) research planets that
            let you improve the capabilities of your other planets and
            military.

ФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФФ
```

```DOC
    ﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄｴ                        ｳ                          ｳ
      ﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾅﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾁﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄｴ

              ﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄﾄｴ * Different Resource.DAT files for each node      ｳ
```
